The content areas (A) through (M) are addressed in TRN-02 (CPR, first aid, safety, disaster, fire and hot water), TRN-03 (habilitation, Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, documentation and disability-specific training), TRN-04 (abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion, critical incidents, rights and confidentiality) and TRN-05 (medications and AIMS).

definitions.definition: A person who provides direct support to individuals in the CILA and is trained and shown competent under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d) and 115.120.
The agency's initial training, with competency checks, covering 115.320(d)(1)(A) through (M).
Showing, by test, observation or scenario, that the person can apply the training correctly with the individuals served.
The agency's document listing the training offered, the methods for completing it and the process for determining competency.
The agency's plan for ongoing training after orientation.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Training Coordinator [NAME/TITLE] who maintains the written training plan, the training calendar and the training tracking record for all staff.

The written training plan lists each required training topic (A) through (M), who delivers it, the method (classroom, online, hands-on, on-the-job, return demonstration), the hours, the way competence is determined, the renewal interval and the passing standard. The Governing Body or Administrator reviews and updates it at least annually.

Before a new hire, contractual worker or volunteer with direct care responsibility starts, the Training Coordinator checks the person's prior training and experience and records whether the person has previous direct service experience.
On the first day, the Training Coordinator assigns the orientation program. The person does not work alone with individuals until orientation is complete and competence is documented.

A person with no previous direct-service experience works only alongside trained staff who are on site and available for on-the-job training until competence is documented in the employee record. The trainer signs and dates each competency.

Competence in each topic is verified by written test, direct observation, return demonstration or scenario. Failing a competency requires retraining and a repeat check before the person works unsupervised in that area. Results are recorded on the competency checklist.

Anyone who provides direct care more than 20% of the time completes DSP training (DD Aide) through a DDD-approved program before working alone, and the Training Coordinator reports completion to the Health Care Worker Registry as required. The Training Coordinator reviews schedules quarterly to identify anyone who passes the 20% threshold.

The Training Coordinator tracks CPR, first aid and OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training expiration dates and schedules retraining before the two-year renewal date. A person whose certification lapses is not counted for coverage that requires the certification until it is renewed.

The Administrator ensures that enough staff are fully trained, including in medication, CPR and first aid, to cover expected and unexpected absences. The Training Coordinator reviews the coverage roster each quarter.

The Training Coordinator, with the QIDP, trains each employee on the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy of the individuals they will support before the employee works with them, and again when a plan changes (TRN-03).

After orientation, each direct service employee has an individual development plan under the agency's employee development plan, reviewed at the annual performance review. It addresses identified skill gaps, new individual needs, changes in regulation, and refresher topics.

Ongoing development activities are scheduled at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., quarterly] and may include in-service sessions, nurse-led health training, behavior support updates and DDD or provider association offerings. Attendance is recorded with the date, topic, trainer and hours.

The Training Coordinator places training and competence documentation in each employee's personnel record (STF-05) and keeps a summary tracker at the agency office. Volunteers' records are kept under VOL-01.
On request or during a visit, the Administrator makes all training records readily available to BALC and DDD, in person or electronically, within the same day.
After IMPACT enrollment, the Administrator submits the agency's DSP and QIDP training programs to DDD for approval and keeps DDD's approval on file. Program changes are submitted to DDD before use.

The Training Coordinator reports training completion rates, overdue items and failed competencies to the Administrator monthly. The Quality Assurance Plan (QA-01) reviews these data at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures resources for training and receives training compliance reports.
Ensures the written training plan is implemented, coverage for absences is adequate, DDD approvals are obtained and records are available to BALC and DDD.
Maintains the training plan, schedules and tracks training, verifies competency documentation and reports completion to the Health Care Worker Registry as required.
Trains staff on each individual's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy and checks competence.
Delivers or oversees health and medication training and competency checks.

responsibilities.role: Direct support staff, contractual workers and volunteers
responsibilities.duty: Complete training, show competence, take part in development activities and work unsupervised only after being cleared.

documentation: Written training plan and annual review record
New-hire orientation checklist and competency checklist signed and dated by trainer and trainee
Tests, observation forms and scenario results
Certificates for DSP training, CPR/first aid and OIG Rule 50 training, with expiration dates
Employee development plans and in-service attendance records
Training tracking spreadsheet or system report
DDD approval of DSP and QIDP training programs
Coverage roster for absences
Records of reporting to the Health Care Worker Registry

policies.title: CPR, First Aid, Choking Response, Safety, Disaster, Fire and Hot Water Temperature Training
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, paraprofessionals, contractual workers and volunteers with direct care responsibility; the Training Coordinator, Administrator and Nurse
policies.purpose: To ensure every direct care worker can respond to medical and safety emergencies, evacuate individuals, use fire equipment and keep hot water at safe temperatures.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d)(1)(A) (cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), back blows/abdominal thrusts, and first aid), 115.320(d)(1)(C) (safety and disaster procedures, public health emergencies, fire procedures and the use of fire equipment such as a fire extinguisher) and 115.320(d)(1)(L) (techniques for monitoring and regulating hot water temperatures before and during an individual's use for safe hand-washing, hair-washing, bathing and showering, with water between 100 and 110 degrees). Staff show competence in these areas during orientation and before unsupervised responsibility for direct service. CPR, choking response and first aid training is renewed every two years. Staff and individuals are trained in the site's emergency procedures, including fire, severe weather, missing persons, medical and psychiatric emergencies, poison control and death. New individuals are trained on these procedures within 30 days of moving in (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Staff are trained in the location of fire extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes at each site where they work. Staff protect themselves and individuals from exposure to blood and body fluids under 29 CFR 1910.1030.

definitions.definition: Techniques used to clear an obstructed airway in a choking person.
An event such as an outbreak of communicable disease that requires changes in infection control, staffing, visiting or services.
Water delivered to hand-washing, hair-washing, bathing and showering fixtures between 100 and 110 degrees Fahrenheit.
A practice in which staff and individuals actually leave the building to a safe area, as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300.

procedures: The Training Coordinator enrolls each new direct care worker in a CPR, back blows/abdominal thrusts and first aid course taught by a nationally recognized provider that includes hands-on skills practice and testing. The worker completes it during orientation, before working alone.

The Training Coordinator records each certification date and expiration date. Renewal is scheduled before the two-year date, and the worker is not counted as the sole certified person on a shift once the certification lapses.

At each site, the Administrator or designee gives a walk-through to each new worker covering the location of fire extinguishers, first aid kits, evacuation routes, exits, the posted site telephone and poison control numbers, shut-off valves and the emergency binder. The worker signs the walk-through checklist.

Orientation training covers the site's disaster preparedness plan, including fire, severe weather, power loss, missing persons, medical and psychiatric emergencies, poison control, deaths and public health crises. Competence is checked by quiz or scenario.

Staff training on fire procedures includes how to sound the alarm, call 911, remove individuals from danger, close doors, and use an approved fire extinguisher. The trainer demonstrates the use of the extinguisher and the worker shows the steps using a scenario or hands-on practice.

Staff take part in evacuation drills that include actual evacuation to safe areas, and the Training Coordinator records each drill attendance. Corrective actions for any drill or inspection deficiency are recorded and the affected staff are retrained (ENV-01).

Within 30 days of moving in, the QIDP or designee trains each new individual on emergency procedures in a way the person understands, using demonstration and practice, and records the date and the person's response. Training is repeated when the individual's needs or the site's procedures change.

Hot water training covers how to check water temperature with a thermometer or tempering device before and during use, how to adjust the mixing, the 100 to 110 degree safe range, and how to protect individuals who cannot judge temperature or protect themselves. Each worker demonstrates the temperature check at the site.

Staff test hot water at the point of use at [FREQUENCY, e.g., weekly] and whenever a plumbing change or complaint occurs, and record it on the hot water log. Readings outside 100 to 110 degrees are reported to the Administrator the same day. Individuals are not bathed or showered until the water is corrected, and the Administrator arranges repair.
Staff learn to check for first aid kit supplies. Kits meet Red Cross-standard contents and are inspected quarterly and restocked, with each check recorded (ENV-01).

Training on bloodborne pathogens and universal precautions follows 29 CFR 1910.1030 and is completed during orientation and renewed annually, with training on gloves, spill cleanup and sharps (ENV-02).

The Training Coordinator tests competence by return demonstration for CPR and fire extinguisher use, by written test for emergency procedures, and by observation for hot water checks. Any failure triggers retraining and a repeat check.
Records of all training are placed in the personnel file and a summary is kept at each site, where they are available to DDD and BALC. Fire and disaster training records are available at the site.
The Administrator reviews the training tracker each month for expiring certifications and reports gaps to the Governing Body and the quality assurance review (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures every site has certified and trained staff on every shift and that hot water, first aid and fire equipment checks are completed.
Schedules and tracks CPR/first aid renewals, safety, fire and hot water training, and records competence.
Teaches or reviews first aid, choking and medical emergency response, and bloodborne pathogen precautions.
Trains new individuals on emergency procedures within 30 days of move-in and documents it.
Keep certifications current, know the site's emergency procedures and equipment locations, test hot water as assigned and report problems at once.

documentation: CPR, choking and first aid certificates with expiration dates
Site orientation and walk-through checklist signed by the worker
Fire extinguisher, evacuation drill and disaster training attendance and competency records
Individual emergency procedures training record dated within 30 days of move-in
Hot water training competency record and hot water temperature log
First aid kit quarterly inspection log
Bloodborne pathogen training record
Training tracker showing renewal dates

policies.title: Habilitation, Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, Documentation and Disability-Specific Training
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals and other staff with direct care responsibility; QIDP, Training Coordinator and Administrator
policies.purpose: To prepare staff to carry out each individual's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, to document supports accurately and to deliver supports suited to each person's disability and needs.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d)(1)(B) (concepts of habilitation and rehabilitation, including behavior intervention and management, age appropriateness and psycho-social rehabilitation, depending on the needs of the individuals served), 115.320(d)(1)(F) (the purpose and content of the Personal Plan under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(2)), 115.320(d)(1)(G) (development and implementation of an Implementation Strategy), 115.320(d)(1)(J) (documentation and recordkeeping requirements for the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy) and 115.320(d)(1)(K) (other training specific to the type of disability, treatment and intervention techniques used for individuals living in the CILA, to help staff carry out Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy outcomes). Staff show competence in each of these areas during orientation and before unsupervised direct service, and receive added training whenever an individual's plan changes. [AGENCY NAME] develops an Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230 and 120.160). Training emphasizes person-centered, age-appropriate support that builds skills, choice and community integration. Restraint, seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are not used, and training on behavior support addresses positive behavior supports only (GPR-03, GPR-04).

definitions.definition: Supports and instruction that help an individual learn, keep or improve skills for living, working and taking part in the community.
The person-centered plan developed under 42 CFR 441.301(c)(2) and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120 that states the individual's goals, needs and supports.
The agency's plan, on Form IL462-4470, that states how [AGENCY NAME] will carry out the Personal Plan outcomes it agreed to support, including methods, staff, time periods and locations.
Offering activities, materials, language and treatment suited to the individual's chronological age and dignity.
Supports that help a person build social, emotional and coping skills and recover roles in community life.

procedures: During orientation, the QIDP or Training Coordinator teaches the concepts of habilitation and rehabilitation, including how to teach skills in daily routines, use of prompts and reinforcement, age-appropriate respect, psycho-social rehabilitation and positive behavior support. Content is matched to the needs of the individuals the staff will support.

Staff are taught the purpose and content of the Personal Plan, including that it is person-centered, reflects the individual's goals and preferences, is developed with the individual and guardian and identifies services, risks and supports (42 CFR 441.301(c)(2)).

Staff are taught how the Implementation Strategy is developed: the QIDP uses the Personal Plan and assessments, involves the individual and guardian (with the ISC as needed), completes Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, and addresses the outcomes the agency agreed to support.

Staff are taught that the individual and guardian sign the Implementation Strategy and receive a copy of it and each update, that the strategy becomes part of the record and that the QIDP reviews it at least monthly and documents the review.

Staff are taught how the strategy sets the times and places when an individual who needs continuous supervision may stay alone or go into the community independently, that this follows an assessment by the Provider Support Team and is based on need and preference, not staff convenience.

Before working alone with an individual, each employee reads that person's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, is shown the supports by the QIDP or a trained staff member, and signs a form confirming that they have read and understand them. The QIDP checks understanding by questions or observation.

Staff are trained on documentation and recordkeeping: what to record, how to write factual, dated, signed and timely daily notes tied to the outcomes, how to record incidents and refusals, how to correct errors without erasing, and how electronic signatures are used (PCS-03, REC-02). Staff complete a practice entry and the QIDP reviews it.
Staff are taught their role in the cumulative record and confidentiality of the information they record (GPR-01, REC-01).

The QIDP identifies each individual's disability-specific needs, such as autism, Down syndrome with aging, epilepsy, communication devices, mobility and transfer needs, dysphagia and feeding, sensory needs and psychiatric diagnoses. The Training Coordinator arranges training specific to those needs, delivered by the QIDP, Nurse, therapist, behavior specialist or outside trainer, before the staff member supports that person.

Training on any treatment or intervention technique used with an individual, including behavior supports in an approved plan, is completed and competence shown before staff use the technique. The Behavior Management Committee approves the content (GPR-03).

When a Personal Plan or Implementation Strategy is changed, the QIDP trains all staff who support the individual on the change within [NUMBER, e.g., 7] days or before the change takes effect, and records the training.

The Training Coordinator checks competence by observation, scenario or test, and records results. A staff member who does not show competence is retrained and rechecked before working alone on that task.

The Training Coordinator files records of all training in the personnel record and the training tracker, and the QIDP files individual-specific read-and-understand records at the site. These are available to BALC and DDD.
The QIDP observes direct support staff delivering supports at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly] and gives feedback, with results tracked in the quality assurance review (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Teaches staff the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, develops the strategy within 20 calendar days, reviews it monthly, trains staff on changes and checks competence.
Schedules training on habilitation, documentation and disability-specific topics and keeps records.
Ensures staff are cleared for individual-specific supports before working alone and that training resources are available.
Provide training on health-related and disability-specific interventions.
Read and follow each individual's plan and strategy, document daily as trained and report concerns to the QIDP.

documentation: Orientation curriculum and competency checklist for habilitation, Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy and documentation
Signed read-and-understand records for each individual's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
Training sign-in sheets and competency results for disability-specific and intervention techniques
Records of staff training on plan changes
QIDP observation and feedback notes
Implementation Strategy (Form IL462-4470) with dates showing completion within 20 calendar days and monthly QIDP review notes

policies.title: Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation, Coercion, Critical Incident, Rights and Confidentiality Training
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractual workers, volunteers and practitioners with responsibility for direct care; the Training Coordinator, Administrator and QIDP
policies.purpose: To make sure every direct care worker can recognize, prevent, handle and report abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and critical incidents, and respects individual rights and confidentiality.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d)(1)(D) (abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and critical incident prevention, handling and reporting to the DHS OIG under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50) and 115.320(d)(1)(E) (individual rights under Section 115.250 and maintaining confidentiality under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, 740 ILCS 110; the official checklist text cites this Act as 740 ILCS 100, and [AGENCY NAME] applies 740 ILCS 110). Staff complete this training during orientation and show competence before unsupervised direct service. OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training is renewed every two years, and [AGENCY NAME] also refreshes rights and confidentiality training at least annually. Abuse, neglect and exploitation are defined as in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.10 as adopted in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Staff must report any suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation in the manner and within the time required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50 and the agency's reporting policies (GPR-05, CI-02). The agency notifies the guardian or parent of an abuse or neglect allegation within 24 hours of receiving it. Training explains the rights stated in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250, including the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201), which is shared and explained at entry and annually, the right to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint, the prohibition on seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures, and the individual's right to contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's OIG, the Department and the agency's human rights committee.

definitions.definition: Have the meanings in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.10, as adopted by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: pressuring or forcing an individual to act or not act against their will, including through threats or loss of something the person is entitled to.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, including abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50 and other events the rule lists.
Records and communications protected by the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, 740 ILCS 110.
Each staff member, volunteer or contractual worker who must report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation under Part 50 and agency policy.

procedures: The Training Coordinator enrolls every new direct care worker, contractor and volunteer in the OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training approved for the agency before the person works alone with individuals, and verifies a certificate or completion record.

Training covers definitions of abuse, neglect, exploitation and coercion as defined in Part 50 and 115.120, signs and indicators, risk factors and how to prevent them through respectful support, supervision, boundaries and staffing (STF-06).

Training covers each worker's duty to report immediately to the supervisor on duty and to report to the DHS OIG, law enforcement or other required authority as required by Part 50. Staff are taught the steps and timelines in GPR-05 and CI-02, including that reports cannot be delayed to ask a supervisor for approval and that retaliation against a reporter is prohibited.

Training covers protection of the individual after an allegation, preserving evidence, not interviewing the individual beyond what is needed for safety, documentation of facts and cooperation with investigators, and the agency's duty to notify the guardian or parent within 24 hours of receiving an allegation.

Training covers critical incident recognition, handling and reporting (CI-01, CI-02), including missing persons, deaths, serious injuries, restraint use and allegations, using the incident forms and reporting channels, and who to call after hours.

Training on rights reviews the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201), the rights in 115.250, protection under Chapter II of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code, the right to remain in the CILA unless the individual withdraws or meets the discharge criteria, the right to private physicians and professionals of choice, and the ban on seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures. Rights restrictions require due process (RTS-02).

Staff are taught how to help individuals who want to contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the DHS OIG, the Department or the agency's Human Rights Committee, including offering to help, and the location of the posted address and telephone number list for each: [GAC ADDRESS/PHONE], [EQUIP FOR EQUALITY ADDRESS/PHONE], [OIG ADDRESS/PHONE], [DEPARTMENT ADDRESS/PHONE], [HRC CONTACT].

Training on coercion covers how pressure, threats, withholding of preferred items or choices, and staff convenience-based rules can amount to coercion, and how to offer choices and decision-making support instead (RTS-03).

Confidentiality training covers 740 ILCS 110, the agency's privacy practices, what may be shared and with whom, written consent for releases of information, secure handling of paper and electronic records, text messaging and social media restrictions, and the minimum necessary standard (REC-01, RTS-05). It also covers privacy practices under 45 CFR 164.530 where the agency is a covered entity.

Competence is shown by a written test with a passing score of [PERCENT, e.g., 80%], direct observation or a scenario-based exercise in which the worker identifies a reportable event, states who to call, and explains how to protect the individual. The trainer records the method and results in the personnel file.
Failing a test or scenario requires retraining and retesting before the worker has unsupervised responsibility.

The Training Coordinator tracks the two-year OIG Rule 50 renewal date and schedules retraining at least [NUMBER, e.g., 60] days before expiration. Annual rights and confidentiality refreshers are recorded with the date and topics.
Rights materials are shared with individuals and guardians at entry and annually, and the QIDP records the date and method and confirms that the individual understood (RTS-01).
The Administrator reviews incident and complaint trends and adds training topics when data show a pattern (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures every direct care worker completes and keeps current abuse, neglect, rights and confidentiality training, and that guardians are notified within 24 hours of an allegation.
Provides or arranges the training, tests competence, tracks the two-year renewal and files records.
Shares and explains the Rights of Individuals form at entry and annually and helps individuals reach advocacy contacts.
Oversees confidentiality training content and handles questions on releases of information.
Complete the training, report suspected abuse, neglect and exploitation immediately as required and protect confidentiality.

documentation: Certificate or record of OIG Rule 50 abuse and neglect training with completion and renewal dates
Rights, coercion, critical incident and confidentiality training outlines, sign-in sheets, tests and scenario results
Signed statement by each worker that they understand their duty to report
Record of sharing the Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and annually
Posted contact list for GAC, Equip for Equality, DHS OIG, the Department and the Human Rights Committee
Training tracker and training reports to the quality assurance committee

policies.title: Medication and AIMS Training; Nurse-Trainer Certification of Direct Care Staff
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff who supervise self-administration of medication or administer medication; Nurse-Trainer, Administrator and Training Coordinator
policies.purpose: To make sure direct care staff know the medications prescribed for the individuals they support, can observe and report involuntary movements using the AIMS, and are trained, certified and re-evaluated by a Nurse-Trainer before and while they supervise or give medications.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d)(1)(H) (type, dosage, characteristics, effects and side effects of prescribed medications, with enough trained staff to cover expected and unexpected absences), 115.320(d)(1)(I) (observation using the Abnormal Involuntary Movement Skills (AIMS) of involuntary muscular movement that may indicate tardive dyskinesia) and 115.320(d)(1)(M) (unlicensed direct care employees meeting 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116.40(c), including successful completion of a Department-approved training program provided by a CILA agency Nurse-Trainer, before supervising self-administration of medication or administering medications, and re-evaluation by a Nurse-Trainer at least annually or more often at the registered nurse's discretion, with retraining as needed). Where agency employees provide medical services or medications or supervise their administration, [AGENCY NAME] certifies that this is done under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116. No unlicensed staff member supervises self-administration or administers medication until the Nurse-Trainer has certified the person as competent. The Nurse-Trainer is a registered nurse with an unencumbered Illinois license who has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars. AIMS screening is done at least every six months for each individual on psychotropic medication, and a physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240).

definitions.definition: A registered nurse with an unencumbered Illinois license who has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars and teaches the Department-approved medication training program to direct care staff.
A structured observation and screening tool for involuntary muscular movement that can indicate tardive dyskinesia.
A movement disorder that can result from long-term use of certain psychotropic medications.
A medication prescribed to affect mood, thinking or behavior.
Unlicensed direct care employees who have completed the Department-approved training and been certified by the Nurse-Trainer to supervise self-administration or administer medications.

procedures: The Administrator engages an RN Nurse-Trainer [NAME] with an unencumbered Illinois license who has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars, verifies the license on the Illinois Department of Financial and Professional Regulation (IDFPR) license lookup before the first class and at least annually, and keeps proof of webinar completion on file.

The Training Coordinator schedules each new direct care employee for the Department-approved medication training program taught by the Nurse-Trainer, so that completion occurs before the employee has any responsibility for medications. Staff meet the criteria in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116.40(c) before authorization.

The Nurse-Trainer teaches the course content, which covers the type, dosage, characteristics, effects and side effects of medications prescribed for the individuals served, as well as medication safety, the rights of medication administration, documentation, storage and security, missed doses and errors, and when to call the nurse, physician or 911.

For each individual, the Nurse-Trainer or Nurse gives individual-specific teaching to the staff who support them, including each medication's purpose, dose, route, time, side effects to watch for, interactions, special instructions and the prescriber's contact information. Staff sign that the teaching was received.

The Nurse-Trainer tests knowledge and observes hands-on skills, including return demonstration of medication passes with the Medication Administration Record. Authorization is given only on successful completion of the program and competency checks. The Nurse-Trainer issues a signed written certification and the Training Coordinator files it.

Until certified, the employee does not supervise self-administration or give medications and works only with certified staff available. The shift schedule is built so that a certified staff member is on every shift.

The Administrator, with the Training Coordinator, keeps enough certified staff to cover expected and unexpected absences, with a coverage roster reviewed at least quarterly and a back-up plan, such as an on-call certified person or nurse, when coverage falls short.

Staff are trained in AIMS observation during orientation. The Nurse-Trainer teaches how to recognize and describe involuntary movements of the face, mouth, limbs and trunk and how to report them. Each worker shows the observation steps in a practice session or with a trained observer.

The Nurse or a qualified clinician completes AIMS screening for each individual on psychotropic medication at least every six months and when a new psychotropic starts or the dose changes, with results documented, shared with the physician and filed in the record. Staff report new involuntary movements to the Nurse the same day.

The Nurse confirms that a physician (MD/DO) has examined the individual before a psychotropic starts, and that a physician reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires (HLT-01, HLT-02).

The Nurse-Trainer re-evaluates each authorized staff member at least annually, and sooner at the RN's discretion, such as after a medication error, a change in medication regimen, a concern about performance or a long absence. The re-evaluation includes observation of a medication pass.

If the Nurse-Trainer finds a competency gap, the Nurse-Trainer retrains to the extent needed to ensure competency. The staff member's authority is suspended until the Nurse-Trainer re-certifies, and the Administrator is told.

The Training Coordinator keeps a tracking list of authorized staff, certification dates and the next annual re-evaluation date, and flags upcoming due dates at least [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days ahead. Staff whose re-evaluation is overdue are not scheduled to give or supervise medication until completed.

The agency certifies, through the Administrator, that medical services and medications are provided under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116, and keeps Part 116 compliance records available to BALC and DDD.

The Administrator reviews medication errors, AIMS results and certification status monthly in quality assurance (QA-01). Errors that meet the definition of a critical incident are reported under CI-01 and CI-02.

responsibilities.duty: Holds an unencumbered Illinois license, completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars, teaches the Department-approved program, certifies staff and re-evaluates them at least annually.
Provides individual-specific medication teaching, ensures AIMS screening every six months for individuals on psychotropics and coordinates physician reviews.
Ensures only certified staff supervise or administer medications, maintains coverage for absences and certifies compliance with Part 116.
Schedules training and re-evaluations, tracks certification dates and files records.
Follow medication procedures as trained, perform AIMS observations, report errors, side effects and involuntary movements immediately and keep certification current.

documentation: Nurse-Trainer's Illinois license verification and proof of DHS/DDD RN trainer webinar completion
Course roster, curriculum and test results for the Department-approved medication training program
Nurse-Trainer's signed certification for each staff member
Individual-specific medication teaching records
Annual re-evaluation and retraining records
AIMS screening results at least every six months for individuals on psychotropic medication
Medication coverage roster and tracker of authorizations
Agency certification of compliance with the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116

policies.title: Volunteer Orientation, Training and Supervision
policies.applies_to: All volunteers, the Volunteer Coordinator, site supervisors, QIDPs and the Administrator at every [AGENCY NAME] CILA site
policies.purpose: To make sure every volunteer is oriented, trained for the specific duties assigned, supervised, and checked against the required registries before contact with individuals. Volunteers who take on any responsibility for the care of individuals must also demonstrate competency in the same training areas required of direct support professionals.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(e) (Volunteer training). [AGENCY NAME] provides an orientation and training program for volunteers that is specific to the volunteer's duties, and provides supervision as necessary. A volunteer with responsibility for the care of individuals served completes, and demonstrates competency in, all of the training areas in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(d). Those areas are carried out through TRN-01. Before a volunteer starts, the agency checks the DPH Health Care Worker Registry and the DCFS State Central Register/CANTS as required by 115.320(b) and STF-02. The inquiry may not be made more than 30 calendar days before the volunteer's first day, and checks are repeated so that they are completed every 365 days. A volunteer is never left alone with an individual unless the volunteer has completed the required training and the required checks. A volunteer is not counted toward staffing patterns or continuous supervision (STF-04). Volunteers do not administer medication, perform or take part in restraint, or manage an individual's funds. Volunteers do not provide personal care unless they have completed and demonstrated the related competency. The agency keeps a volunteer file for each volunteer that records hours and training.

definitions.definition: A person who provides unpaid services or assistance at or for a CILA site or its individuals and is not an employee or contractual worker of [AGENCY NAME].

A volunteer whose assigned duties include direct assistance, support or supervision of an individual, such as mealtime help, personal assistance, community outings or transportation. Such volunteers must meet the 115.320(d) training and competency requirements.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, the paid staff who provide direct support to individuals. DSP competency standards are the benchmark for volunteers who have care responsibility.

As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, staff physically on-site during all hours individuals are present unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy state otherwise. Volunteers do not satisfy this requirement.

procedures: The Administrator names a Volunteer Coordinator ([VOLUNTEER COORDINATOR]). The Coordinator receives and screens volunteer applications and keeps the volunteer files.

Before accepting a volunteer, the Coordinator writes a short duty description. It states the tasks, sites, hours, the supervising staff member, and whether the role involves responsibility for the care of individuals.

The Coordinator completes the Health Care Worker Registry and DCFS State Central Register/CANTS checks (STF-02) before the volunteer's first day. The inquiry date must be no more than 30 calendar days before that day. The Coordinator also confirms the results have been received. The volunteer does not start until the results are in the file.
The Coordinator calendars each volunteer's repeat checks so that they are completed every 365 days. A volunteer whose repeat check is overdue is suspended from activity until the check is completed.

The Coordinator or a qualified supervisor delivers a documented orientation before the first assignment. It covers the agency's mission, the individuals' rights and the Rights of Individuals form, confidentiality, abuse/neglect/exploitation recognition and reporting (GPR-05, TRN-04), professional boundaries (STF-06), emergency and fire response (ENV-01) and the volunteer's specific duties.

For a volunteer with responsibility for care, the Coordinator and the site supervisor schedule and deliver every training area in 115.320(d) as set out in TRN-01. A trainer observes the volunteer demonstrate each skill. The trainer signs and dates the competency checklist.

Before a volunteer has any unsupervised contact with individuals, the Coordinator verifies that the checks are complete, that orientation is complete, and that competency has been demonstrated for the assigned duties. A volunteer who does not meet all three conditions works only with a staff member physically present and directly observing.

The site supervisor gives each volunteer an individual-specific briefing before the volunteer works with an individual. The briefing covers communication methods, health or safety risks, dietary or choking precautions, behavior supports and any rights restrictions that affect the volunteer's tasks, limited to what the volunteer needs to know.
Each volunteer signs in and out on the volunteer log at the site. The log records the date, hours, tasks and the supervising staff member.

The supervising staff member observes the volunteer, corrects problems on the spot and reports concerns to the Coordinator the same day. The Coordinator may restrict, retrain or end a volunteer's service at any time.

A volunteer who observes or suspects abuse, neglect or exploitation, or any critical incident, reports it immediately to the site supervisor on duty or the on-call supervisor (CI-01, CI-02). The volunteer does not investigate and does not delay the report.

Volunteers who need refresher training or new competencies because of a change in duties or an individual's needs are trained and checked off before they take on the new task. The Coordinator records this in the volunteer file.

At least annually, the Coordinator reviews each active volunteer's file for current registry checks, training, hours and supervisor feedback. The Coordinator reports the results to the Administrator for the quality assurance review (QA-01).
When a volunteer leaves, the Coordinator records the end date and reason in the file and removes any access to the site, records or keys.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the Volunteer Coordinator, approves the volunteer program and ensures resources for orientation, training and supervision.
Screens volunteers, completes and calendars registry checks, schedules orientation and competency training, keeps volunteer files and logs and reports on the program to the Administrator.
Directly supervises volunteers, provides individual-specific briefings, observes competency, and reports concerns to the Coordinator.

Completes all required checks and training, stays within assigned duties, follows rights and confidentiality requirements, and reports incidents and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation immediately.

documentation: Volunteer file: application, duty description, registry check dates and results, orientation record, competency checklists and signed training records
Volunteer sign-in/sign-out log showing hours, tasks and supervising staff member
Individual-specific briefing record
Annual volunteer file review and any retraining or restriction notes

policies.title: Written Quality Assurance Plan, Data Review and Mortality Review
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, QIDPs, nursing oversight, Quality Assurance Committee and all CILA sites operated by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To keep a written quality assurance (QA) plan and ongoing QA activities that review and evaluate services to individuals and the operation of each program, resolve problems that are found, and confirm that individuals receive appropriate services consistent with their Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(f)(1) (Quality assurance). [AGENCY NAME] maintains a written quality assurance plan and ongoing activities designed to review and evaluate services to individuals and the operation of programs and to resolve identified problems. The QA program is the basis for determining that individuals receive appropriate community-based services consistent with their Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies, and that all programs and services are supervised by the agency and comply with 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115. QA findings and resulting actions go to the governing body (GOV-01). The QA plan is reviewed at least annually and revised when the data show a need. Deficiencies found through QA are corrected under QA-02.

definitions.definition: The written plan that states what [AGENCY NAME] measures, how often, who is responsible, what thresholds trigger action, and how results are reported and used.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, and including abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50 as adopted by that section.
A documented review of each death of an individual to identify circumstances, care provided, possible contributing factors and any changes needed in supports, training or procedures.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, the document developed from the Personal Plan and assessments that describes how the agency will support the outcomes it agreed to support.

procedures: The governing body adopts the written QA plan and designates a QA Committee. At minimum the Committee includes the Administrator ([ADMINISTRATOR NAME]), a QIDP, a nurse, a site supervisor and the Authorized CILA Agency Representative.
The QA plan identifies each indicator reviewed, the data source, the person responsible, the review frequency and the threshold that triggers a corrective action.

The QA plan requires review of: critical incident trends (CI-01), rights complaints and grievances (GPR-06), medication errors and nursing findings (HLT-01, HLT-02), record audits (REC-03), restraint or rights-restriction use (GPR-04, RTS-02), staff training and registry-check currency (STF-02, TRN-01), life-safety and drill results (ENV-01), and individual and guardian feedback (GOV-02).
Each month the QIDP for each site reviews the Implementation Strategy and daily documentation (PCS-03) and reports gaps between supports delivered and the plan to the QA Committee.

Each quarter, the QA Committee meets and reviews the data for each site. It compares results to the prior quarter and to the thresholds. It records findings, decisions, assigned corrective actions and due dates in meeting minutes.

The QA Coordinator ([QA COORDINATOR]) audits a sample of individual records each quarter. The audit covers current Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, signatures, consents, the Rights of Individuals form, health records and documentation completeness (REC-03). Missing items are corrected within a time set in the audit.

At least semi-annually, the QA Coordinator runs a mock site inspection of each residence against Part 115 requirements, including the environment, postings, fire extinguisher tags, first aid kits, drill records and the individuals' rights. Findings enter the corrective action log (QA-02).

For each death, the QA Committee completes a mortality review under CI-04. The review covers the care provided, preceding health changes, emergency response and contributing factors. The committee also records any systemic recommendations.

The QA Committee seeks input from individuals, guardians and representatives and reviews that input (GOV-02). It asks them whether services match their Personal Plan and preferences. Their comments are logged with the response given.

The QA Committee sends critical incident trend reports to the Human Rights Committee (GPR-02) and the Behavior Management Committee (GPR-03) when the data involve rights, restraint or behavior supports.

If the data show that a person is not receiving services consistent with the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, the QA Coordinator notifies the QIDP and Administrator immediately. The QIDP corrects the service gap and informs the individual and guardian.

The Administrator presents a written QA report to the governing body at least quarterly. It includes findings, trends, corrective actions and their status, and any recommendation for resources. The governing body's action is recorded in its minutes (GOV-01).
Once a year, the QA Committee reviews the effectiveness of the QA plan itself, revises it as needed, and submits the revision to the governing body for approval.
The Administrator keeps QA records available for BALC and Department review at survey.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts the QA plan, reviews QA reports at least quarterly, directs action on findings and provides resources.
Oversees the QA program, chairs or designates the chair of the QA Committee, and presents reports to the governing body.
Collects data, conducts record audits and mock inspections, maintains the corrective action log and prepares reports.
Reviews Implementation Strategies and documentation monthly, and corrects gaps between supports and the plan.
Supplies medication and health data for QA review and takes part in mortality reviews.
Provide accurate records and incident reports, take part in audits and carry out corrective actions assigned to them.

documentation: Written QA plan with annual review and governing body approval
QA Committee meeting minutes, data summaries and trend reports
Quarterly record audit tools and results
Mock inspection reports and corrective action log (QA-02)
Mortality review reports
Quarterly QA report to the governing body and the governing body's minutes

policies.title: Correction of Deficiencies and Withdrawal of CILA Certification
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, QA Committee, site supervisors and QIDPs for all certified CILAs operated by [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure the quality assurance program is the basis for determining that individuals receive appropriate community-based services, that every deficiency in a certified CILA is corrected within 30 days, and that certification is withdrawn, the Department notified and the individuals protected when a deficiency cannot be corrected in that time.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(f)(2) (Quality assurance program as the basis for determining services) and (f)(2)(A) and (B). [AGENCY NAME]'s quality assurance program is the basis for determining under its license that individuals are receiving appropriate community-based services consistent with their Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies, and that all programs and services are supervised by the agency and comply with 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115. Under (f)(2)(A), if a certified CILA does not continue to meet standards, [AGENCY NAME] corrects the deficiencies within 30 days. Under (f)(2)(B), if the deficiencies cannot be corrected within 30 days, [AGENCY NAME] withdraws certification of the CILA program in question, notifies the Department, and remains responsible for the affected individuals until they have transitioned to other settings. During any withdrawal and transition the agency continues to protect the individuals' rights described in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250, including the Rights of Individuals form and access to the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of Inspector General, the Department and the agency's human rights committee.

definitions.definition: Any condition at a certified CILA that does not meet a requirement of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115, a licensing or certification condition, or the individual's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. It may be identified by a BALC survey, complaint, inspection, mock inspection, record audit or incident review.
A documented action taken to eliminate a deficiency and prevent recurrence, with a responsible person, due date and verification of completion.
The agency's action under 115.320(f)(2)(B) to stop operating a specific CILA program as a certified CILA when its deficiencies cannot be corrected within 30 days.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, the agency official authorized to act for the agency with the Department.

procedures: Any staff member who sees a condition that does not meet a standard reports it to the site supervisor the same day. If the condition places an individual at risk, the supervisor takes protective action immediately and contacts the Administrator.

The QA Coordinator opens an entry in the corrective action log within one business day of identifying a deficiency, from any source. The entry records the date identified, the source, the site, the standard involved and the individuals affected.

The Administrator assigns a responsible person and sets a correction due date. The due date is no later than 30 days after the deficiency was identified. For serious risks to health or safety, the correction is made immediately.
The responsible person writes a corrective action plan within five business days. It states the steps, the person responsible for each step, the due dates and how completion will be verified.

The QA Coordinator reviews progress weekly. At day 15, the Administrator reviews every open item and decides whether it will be corrected within 30 days. Open items are reported to the governing body Chair.

The responsible person records the date of completion and attaches proof, such as a repair invoice, a signed training record, a revised record or a photograph. The QA Coordinator checks the correction in person or by record review before closing the entry.
For corrections tied to individual supports, the QIDP updates the Implementation Strategy or related record and notifies the individual and guardian of the change.

If a deficiency has not been corrected by day 25, the Administrator informs the governing body and the Authorized CILA Agency Representative in writing. The governing body decides whether the deficiency can be fully corrected by day 30. If it cannot, the governing body starts the withdrawal process.

If a deficiency cannot be corrected within 30 days, the governing body records its decision to withdraw certification of the affected CILA program. The Administrator then notifies the Department (BALC and DDD) in writing. The notice states the site, the deficiencies, the actions taken and the planned dates for transition. The agency sends the notice no later than the next business day after the decision.

On withdrawal, the QIDPs notify each affected individual and guardian in person and in writing and explain the options and their rights. The notice includes the address and telephone number of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, the Department's Office of Inspector General, the Department and Equip for Equality. Staff offer help in contacting them.

The agency remains responsible for each affected individual until the person has transitioned to another setting. The QIDP coordinates with the ISC, the guardian, the individual and the receiving provider under PCS-05, and the agency continues to provide the supports in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy until the move is complete.

The agency keeps the site's staffing, health care, medication, safety and rights protections at the required level during the withdrawal and transition period. It records each day's status in the case records.

The Administrator notifies the Department of any ownership change within 60 business days as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.410. Before filing the renewal application, which is due at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice, the Administrator reviews the corrective action log to confirm that no deficiency remains open.

The QA Coordinator tests the corrected area again at the next quarterly review and at the next mock inspection to verify the correction was sustained. Repeat deficiencies are reported to the governing body with a root cause analysis (QA-01).
The Administrator keeps the corrective action log, correspondence with BALC and DDD, and records of any withdrawal and transition available for Department review.

responsibilities.duty: Reviews open deficiencies, decides on withdrawal of certification when deficiencies cannot be corrected in 30 days, and approves resources for correction.
Assigns responsible persons and due dates, monitors the 30-day deadline, notifies the Department of any withdrawal and oversees the transition of individuals.
Maintains the corrective action log, verifies corrections and reports status to the QA Committee.
Updates affected Implementation Strategies, informs individuals and guardians, and coordinates any transition.
Reports deficiencies, takes immediate protective action and carries out corrections at the site.

documentation: Corrective action log with identification date, source, plan, due date, completion date and verification
Corrective action plans and proof of completion
Governing body minutes on deficiencies and any withdrawal decision
Written notice to the Department (BALC and DDD) and related correspondence
Notices to individuals and guardians and transition records (PCS-05)
Mock inspection reports and follow-up verification records

policies.title: Critical Incident Handling, Investigation, Tracking and Analysis
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractual workers and volunteers; supervisors; the Administrator and the Authorized CILA Agency Representative
policies.purpose: To make sure every critical incident is handled promptly, investigated, reported, tracked and analyzed through the agency's management structure, up to and including the Authorized CILA Agency Representative, and that employees demonstrate knowledge of and follow these procedures.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(g)(1) (Critical incidents: written policies and procedures for handling, investigating, reporting, tracking and analyzing critical incidents). [AGENCY NAME] handles every critical incident through its management structure, up to and including the Authorized CILA Agency Representative ([AUTHORIZED CILA AGENCY REPRESENTATIVE NAME]). Critical incidents are those listed under Critical Incidents in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. They include abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50 (59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.10, as adopted in 115.120). The agency keeps a Critical Incident Category List reproduced from the current text of 115.120 at each site. Employees demonstrate their knowledge of these procedures during orientation and annually (TRN-04), and they follow them. External reports are made under CI-02. Missing-person events follow CI-03 and deaths follow CI-04. The first priority is always the safety and medical care of the individual. No one may delay a report to complete an internal review.

definitions.definition: As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, including abuse, neglect and exploitation as defined in Part 50. The agency's site list reproduces the 115.120 categories.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, the person authorized to act for [AGENCY NAME] with the Department. In this policy, the top of the management chain for critical incidents.
As defined in Part 50 of Title 59 and incorporated in 115.120. Staff use the definitions on the site category list and the agency's training (TRN-04).
The agency's central record of all critical incidents with date, site, individual, type, reports made, investigation status, outcome and corrective actions.

procedures: The staff member who witnesses or learns of an incident first ensures the safety of the individual and others and obtains medical care or calls 911 when needed (HLT-03).

The staff member notifies the site supervisor, or the on-call supervisor if none is on site, immediately. The supervisor decides whether the event is a critical incident by using the site Critical Incident Category List. When unsure, the event is treated as a critical incident.

If abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, or a possible crime has occurred, the staff member and supervisor follow CI-02 and GPR-05 at once. The agency's reports to the Office of Inspector General and law enforcement are not delayed for any internal step.

The supervisor notifies the Administrator immediately when an incident involves abuse, neglect, exploitation, a death, a restraint, an injury needing hospital care, a missing person or a law enforcement response. The Administrator informs the Authorized CILA Agency Representative the same day.

The staff member who witnessed or learned of the incident completes the written incident report before the end of the shift. It gives facts only: who, what, when, where, the individuals and staff involved, witnesses, injuries, actions taken and who was notified.
The supervisor reviews the report within 24 hours, confirms that the individual is safe, that the guardian has been notified when required, and that each external report has been made and recorded.

The Administrator assigns an investigator who was not involved in the incident and is not the subject of any allegation. For suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the agency cooperates with, and does not interfere with, any investigation by the Office of Inspector General or law enforcement. The agency takes whatever protective steps they direct, including keeping staff away from the individual when needed.

The investigator interviews staff and witnesses, reviews records and the scene, and completes a written report within [INVESTIGATION DEADLINE - e.g., 14] calendar days unless an outside agency directs otherwise. The report states the findings, the cause or contributing factors and recommended actions.
The Administrator and the Authorized CILA Agency Representative review the investigative report, decide on corrective and personnel actions, and sign off on the final disposition.

The QIDP reviews each affected individual's Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy for needed changes and convenes the provider support team when supports must change (PCS-02). Incidents tied to behavior are sent to the Behavior Management Committee (GPR-03).

The QA Coordinator enters each incident in the incident tracking log within one business day. The entry shows the date, site, individual, category, reports made and report dates, investigation status, final outcome and corrective actions.

Each month the QA Coordinator analyzes the log by site, individual, category, time of day, staff and location. The QA Coordinator looks for patterns and unresolved items and gives the analysis to the Administrator.

Each quarter, the QA Committee reviews the trend analysis and adopts prevention measures such as retraining, supervision changes, environmental repairs or plan changes (QA-01). The analysis is shared with the Human Rights Committee (GPR-02) and the governing body (GOV-01).

All employees demonstrate knowledge of this policy at orientation and at least annually by a signed competency check (TRN-04). Supervisors verify that new staff know where the Category List, forms and on-call numbers are posted.
Incident reports and investigation files are kept confidential in a secure location apart from the individual's routine record. Access is limited to those who need it (REC-01).

responsibilities.duty: Protect the individual, report incidents immediately and in writing before the end of the shift, and follow this policy.
Confirm the category, make or confirm required notifications, review the report within 24 hours and escalate to the Administrator.
Assigns the investigator, reviews findings, directs corrective action and keeps the Authorized CILA Agency Representative informed.
Receives escalated critical incidents, approves final dispositions and represents the agency to the Department.
Maintains the tracking log and prepares monthly and quarterly analyses.

documentation: Written incident reports and investigation reports
Incident tracking log
Notification records (guardian, law enforcement, OIG, CIRAS)
Corrective action records and Implementation Strategy updates
Monthly and quarterly trend analyses and QA Committee minutes
Staff competency checks on this policy

policies.title: Reporting to Law Enforcement, DHS OIG and CIRAS
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractual workers and volunteers; supervisors; the Administrator and the Authorized CILA Agency Representative
policies.purpose: To make sure that incidents are reported to the correct outside authority within the required time: law enforcement within 24 hours for criminal incidents, the Office of Inspector General within four hours of discovery for suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, and DDD through CIRAS for all other critical incidents.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(g)(2), (g)(3) and (g)(4). Under (g)(2), within 24 hours of occurrence [AGENCY NAME] reports any incident subject to the Criminal Code of 2012 [720 ILCS 5] to the local law enforcement agency. Under (g)(3), [AGENCY NAME] reports suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation against individuals to the Department's Office of Inspector General (OIG) within four hours of discovery. Under (g)(4), incidents other than those required to be reported to OIG are reported electronically to DDD through the Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System (CIRAS). The incidents to be reported are those specified under Critical Incidents in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Abuse, neglect and exploitation have the Part 50 meanings adopted in 115.120. The guardian or parent of an individual is notified of an abuse or neglect allegation within 24 hours of the agency's receiving it (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320). Any use of restraint is reported in CIRAS and to OIG, and prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245). Any staff member may make a report. No supervisor may stop, delay or screen out a report. Staff who make reports in good faith are protected from retaliation.

definitions.definition: The moment any employee, contractual worker or volunteer first sees, hears or learns of facts that suggest abuse, neglect or exploitation. The four-hour OIG clock starts at that moment, not when a supervisor is told.
The time an incident subject to the Criminal Code of 2012 happened. The 24-hour law enforcement clock starts then.
DDD's Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System, the electronic system for critical incident reports.
The Department of Human Services Office of Inspector General, which receives reports of suspected abuse, neglect and exploitation of individuals in programs licensed by the Department.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited under 115.245, and seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are prohibited under 115.250.

procedures: The staff member who discovers suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation makes sure the individual is safe and gets medical care, then reports to OIG by the OIG hotline at [OIG HOTLINE NUMBER] immediately and in every case within four hours of discovery. The staff member does not wait for a supervisor's approval.

The staff member also tells the site supervisor or on-call supervisor immediately. If the supervisor learns of suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation first, the supervisor confirms that the OIG report was made. If it was not, the supervisor makes it at once and inside the four-hour limit.

The person who makes the OIG report records the date, time, the name of the OIG staff member who took the report, the OIG report or reference number and the instructions given. The person enters this on the incident report.

If the incident may be a crime under the Criminal Code of 2012 [720 ILCS 5], such as battery, theft, sexual assault, or criminal damage, the supervisor calls 911 if there is immediate danger. Otherwise, the supervisor calls the local law enforcement agency, [LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT NUMBER], within 24 hours of the occurrence. The supervisor records the date, time, agency, officer name and report number.

Staff preserve the scene and any evidence. They do not clean, alter or discard anything and do not interview the individual beyond what is needed for safety and medical care. Staff do not question the person suspected of the act.

The supervisor notifies the guardian or parent of an abuse or neglect allegation within 24 hours of the agency's receiving the allegation, and records the date, time, person reached and what was said. If the guardian cannot be reached, the supervisor documents each attempt and keeps trying until contact is made (GPR-05).

For any other critical incident listed under Critical Incidents in 115.120 that is not required to go to OIG, the supervisor or QA Coordinator enters the report in CIRAS as soon as the person is safe and the facts are known. The agency's standard is no later than the end of the next business day, or sooner if CIRAS instructions require it. The agency keeps the CIRAS confirmation with the incident file.

Any use of restraint is reported in CIRAS and to OIG. The supervisor makes both reports and records them. The supervisor also reports any use of a prohibited restraint (prone, supine or mechanical) as a suspected rights violation. The Administrator is notified at once (GPR-04).

If an event involves both a possible crime and suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation, the agency makes every required report. The OIG report is within four hours of discovery and the law enforcement report is within 24 hours of occurrence. A report to one agency does not replace a report to another.

If CIRAS or the OIG hotline cannot be reached, the supervisor keeps trying and records each attempt. The supervisor notifies the Administrator immediately, who contacts DDD or OIG by another channel. The agency completes the report as soon as the system or line is available.

The Administrator checks that every required external report was made. The Administrator reviews each incident file within two business days against a reporting checklist covering law enforcement, OIG, CIRAS, guardian notice and any other notification. Any late or missing report is corrected at once. It is then treated as a deficiency and entered in the QA corrective action log (QA-02).
The Authorized CILA Agency Representative is told about every OIG report, law enforcement report, restraint report and death the same day (CI-01).

The agency posts the current OIG hotline number and the other contact numbers given to individuals under 115.250 at each site in a place accessible to individuals. The Administrator confirms the numbers with the Department each year and whenever notified of a change before printing new postings.

The agency cooperates fully with OIG and law enforcement investigations. It gives them access to records, staff and individuals as the law allows, and follows their directions about protective actions. The agency makes no contact that could interfere with an investigation (CI-01).

The QA Coordinator tracks report timeliness each quarter, including the time between discovery and the OIG report, occurrence and law enforcement report, and the CIRAS entry date. Results go to the QA Committee (QA-01).

responsibilities.role: All staff, contractual workers and volunteers
responsibilities.duty: Report suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation to OIG within four hours of discovery and tell the supervisor immediately. Do not delay for approval.
Confirm that law enforcement, OIG, CIRAS and guardian notifications are made on time, and record them.
Reviews each incident file for complete and timely reporting, corrects any missed report, and makes sure the numbers are posted.
Is told of all OIG and law enforcement reports, restraints and deaths the same day and acts for the agency with the Department.
Enters CIRAS reports when assigned and tracks the timeliness of all external reports.

documentation: Incident report showing times of discovery or occurrence and each report made
OIG report reference numbers and the name of the person who took the report
Law enforcement report numbers, agency and officer names
CIRAS confirmations
Guardian or parent notification record, including attempts
Reporting checklist review by the Administrator and quarterly timeliness data

policies.title: Missing Person and Elopement
policies.applies_to: All direct support staff, supervisors, QIDPs, the Administrator and on-call personnel at every CILA site
policies.purpose: To ensure staff know how to react immediately when an individual is missing, so that the person is found and kept safe, the guardian and authorities are notified, the incident is reported, and the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy are reviewed afterward.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains staff and individuals on how to react to a missing person, as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300. Each individual's risk and supervision level are set in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy. Time alone and independent access to the community are allowed only as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230 permits. That means they are based on assessment by the provider support team and on the individual's need and preference, not staff convenience, and the Implementation Strategy states the time periods and locations involved. A person is missing when the whereabouts of the person are unknown and the person is outside the time periods, locations or supervision arrangements in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, or when staff have reason to believe the person is in danger. An individual who is away within the plan's stated time and location is not missing. Staff begin an immediate search and make law enforcement, guardian and supervisor notifications as set out below. A missing person event is a critical incident reported under CI-01 and CI-02. If neglect is suspected, it is also reported to the Office of Inspector General. Each record contains a current photo and description of the individual (REC-03). The agency does not use locks, alarms or other measures that restrict an individual's freedom to leave unless a rights restriction has been approved through RTS-02.

definitions.definition: An individual whose whereabouts are unknown and who is outside the supervision arrangements, time periods or locations in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy, or who is believed to be in danger.

An individual whom the Personal Plan or Implementation Strategy identifies as at risk if away, for example due to an inability to recognize danger, a medical condition, a history of elopement, or a need for continuous supervision.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, staff physically on-site during all hours individuals are present, unless the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy state otherwise.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. See CI-01.

procedures: Staff who realize an individual may be missing check the individual's Implementation Strategy at once to see whether the absence falls within the approved time, location or independence arrangement. If it does not, or staff are unsure, treat the person as missing.
The staff member announces the event to the other staff on duty. One staff member stays with the remaining individuals so that they are supervised at all times. No site is left unstaffed.

Staff immediately search the residence, grounds, vehicles, garage, shed, nearby areas and the places the individual is known to frequent. They use the current photo and description kept in the individual's record.

If the individual is high-risk, in danger, a vulnerable person, or has a known condition such as seizures, or if the weather is severe, staff call 911 immediately without waiting for a search to finish. Otherwise, if the individual is not found within 30 minutes of the search starting, staff call 911 or the local law enforcement agency at [LOCAL LAW ENFORCEMENT NUMBER].

Staff give the dispatcher the individual's name, age, physical description, clothing, photo, communication needs, medical needs, risks and the last place and time the person was seen. They record the officer's name and the report number.

Staff notify the site supervisor or on-call supervisor immediately, and no later than the time the search begins. The supervisor then informs the Administrator, who informs the Authorized CILA Agency Representative as soon as possible.

The supervisor notifies the guardian or parent promptly after the search begins. The call is made no later than one hour after the person is found to be missing. The supervisor records the time, the person reached and the information given, and keeps the guardian updated until the person is found.

If staff suspect neglect or another form of abuse or exploitation, such as inadequate supervision, a report to the Office of Inspector General is made within four hours of discovery (CI-02). If the event may be a crime, the law enforcement report is made within 24 hours of occurrence. The event is also reported electronically in CIRAS as a critical incident (CI-02).

When the individual is found, staff make sure the person is safe, check for injuries and get medical care or call 911 as needed (HLT-03). Staff are calm and supportive and do not scold or punish the individual. They notify law enforcement, the guardian, the supervisor and the Administrator that the person has been found.
The nurse or supervisor documents the individual's condition after return. Staff continue to observe the person for the rest of the shift and record any changes in health or behavior.

Within one business day of the return, the QIDP reviews the event and convenes the provider support team (PCS-02) to ask why it happened, such as unmet needs, a trigger, a gap in supervision or an environmental factor. The team reviews the Implementation Strategy, risk level and supervision arrangement, and decides whether supports, training or the environment should change.

Any proposed limit on the individual's freedom to leave or go into the community is handled as a rights restriction with due process, informed consent and committee review (RTS-02, GPR-02) and is not applied informally. The strategy states the time periods and locations involved (115.230).

The supervisor completes the incident report before the end of the shift (CI-01). The QA Coordinator enters the event in the tracking log and includes it in the monthly trend analysis. The QA Committee reviews patterns of missing-person events each quarter (QA-01).

The agency trains staff on this policy at orientation and annually (TRN-02, TRN-04). It includes site-specific drills that practice assigning roles, conducting the search and calling for help. The agency also teaches individuals, in a manner they understand, what to do if they become separated from staff in the community (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300).
