The QIDP verifies every quarter that each record has a current photo and physical description and updates them when the person's appearance changes, and at least annually (REC-03).

responsibilities.duty: Start the search immediately, keep other individuals supervised, call 911 when required, and notify the supervisor.
Direct the search, call law enforcement, notify the guardian, Administrator and OIG when required, and complete the incident report.
Convenes the provider support team after the event, reviews the Implementation Strategy and risk level, and keeps photos and descriptions current.
Ensures all reports are made, informs the Authorized CILA Agency Representative and sees that training and drills are carried out.
Assesses the individual's health after return and advises on medical risks that affect supervision.

documentation: Incident report with the search timeline, the times of calls, and the person's condition when found
Law enforcement report number, guardian notification record, OIG and CIRAS confirmations when applicable
Current photo and description in each individual's record
Provider support team review and any Implementation Strategy revision
Rights restriction documentation if a restriction is proposed (RTS-02)
Training and drill records on missing person response

policies.title: Death of an Individual
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, QIDPs, nurses, supervisors, administrators, volunteers and contractors at every [AGENCY NAME] CILA site
policies.purpose: To make sure that when an individual dies, or is found without signs of life, staff respond immediately and correctly, the family and guardian are notified with compassion, required authorities are informed, evidence and records are protected, and the agency learns from every death through a mortality review.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] trains every staff member how to respond to a death and to other medical emergencies, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300 requires. Staff call 911 and begin CPR unless a valid directive in the individual's record says otherwise. Staff then notify the guardian or emergency contact and the physician. A death is a critical incident under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. The agency reports it in CIRAS as handled in CI-02. When abuse, neglect or exploitation is suspected, the agency also notifies the DHS Office of Inspector General (OIG). The abuse, neglect and financial exploitation definitions in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 50.10 apply, and the guardian or parent is notified within 24 hours of receipt of an abuse or neglect allegation (115.320). Staff preserve the scene and the individual's records. The agency completes a mortality review that feeds the Quality Assurance plan (QA-01). The agency treats the individual, housemates and staff with dignity and offers support after the death.

definitions.definition: An event defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, including a death and abuse, neglect or exploitation as defined in Part 50, that must be handled, investigated, tracked and reported under CI-01 and CI-02.
A current, signed physician order or directive in the individual's record (for example a DNR or POLST) that governs resuscitation and that the individual or guardian has authorized.
The Department's Critical Incident Reporting and Analysis System, used to report critical incidents.
A structured review of the circumstances, care and health history preceding a death, done to find preventable factors and system improvements.
The person the governing body has authorized to act and communicate for [AGENCY NAME] with the Department and other authorities, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120.

procedures: Orientation and annual refresher: The QIDP or designated trainer teaches every staff member, volunteer and contractor with direct contact how to respond to a death, using this policy, and documents the training in the personnel record (see TRN-02).

Posted information: The Site Supervisor keeps an operational telephone at each site. Beside it, the supervisor posts the site address and phone number, the nearest poison control center, the on-call nurse and administrator numbers [PHONE], and the guardian/emergency contact list location.

Recognizing a medical emergency: A staff member who finds an individual unresponsive or not breathing immediately calls 911 and gives the site address. Another staff member (or the caller, if alone, on speaker) starts CPR.

Directives: Before starting CPR, staff check for a valid directive in the individual's record at the site. If a valid directive says no resuscitation, staff do not start CPR. They still call 911 and follow dispatcher and responder instructions. Staff never decide on their own that someone is beyond help.

Safety of others: The staff member in charge makes sure the other individuals at the site are supervised and kept safe, and moves them to a calm area if appropriate. Continuous supervision of the housemates continues without a gap.

Responders: Staff cooperate fully with EMS, law enforcement and the coroner or medical examiner. Staff give the individual's medication list, diagnoses, directive and guardian contact to responders. The Site Supervisor makes sure someone records the responders' names, agencies and arrival and departure times.

Notification of the guardian: Immediately after the emergency response begins, the Site Supervisor or administrator calls the guardian or emergency contact. If the person has been pronounced dead, the call is made by a supervisor or the administrator, not left to a direct support professional alone. The call is made by phone or in person and never by text or voicemail only. The agency records the time and person reached.

Notification of the physician and agency leadership: The Site Supervisor notifies the individual's physician, the agency nurse, the QIDP and [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as soon as the emergency is under control, and documents the time of each call.

Preserving the scene and records: Unless needed for emergency care, staff do not move the individual, clean the area, discard items or alter anything after death. Staff secure the individual's room. They keep medication, MAR, daily notes and personal items unaltered and in place. No one removes or rewrites record entries.

Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation: If anything suggests abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff tell the administrator immediately. The administrator reports to law enforcement and to OIG as directed in GPR-05 and CI-02 and makes sure the guardian or parent is notified within 24 hours of receipt of the allegation. Staff involved in the allegation are removed from direct contact with individuals while the matter is reviewed.

CIRAS and other reports: The authorized CILA agency representative reports the death in CIRAS within the time frames the Department sets, following CI-02. The representative also reports to other agencies and bodies as CI-02 directs and files the reports in the critical incident file.

Release of the body and belongings: The agency releases the body only to the coroner, medical examiner, funeral director or other party that the guardian or legal authority has designated. The Site Supervisor inventories the individual's personal property and funds with a second staff member witnessing. The agency holds them for the guardian or the estate's representative and handles them as required in FIN-03.

Support for housemates and staff: Within 24 hours the QIDP and administrator offer housemates support in the manner they understand, including information in their communication mode, and tell the people the individual designated. The agency offers staff time to debrief and information about counseling resources.

Incident report: The staff member in charge writes a factual incident report before the end of the shift. It states what was observed, the times, actions taken, who was called and who responded. Facts are separated from opinion.

Investigation and follow-up: The administrator assigns an investigation under CI-01 within one business day. The QIDP and nurse gather the record, last physician visit, medications, health risk reviews, and recent changes of condition.

Mortality review: Within [MORTALITY REVIEW TIMEFRAME, e.g., 30 days] of the death, the administrator convenes the QA committee, including the nurse, QIDP and others as needed. The group reviews cause of death (when known), health care provided, staff response, directive compliance, and preventable factors. It documents findings and recommendations.
Corrective action: The administrator assigns corrective actions with a responsible person and due date. QA-01 tracks them to completion, and the results go to the governing body.

Closing the record: The QIDP completes discharge documentation by following PCS-05 and notifies the Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency and the Department as required. The record then moves to retention under REC-04.

responsibilities.duty: Call 911, start CPR unless a valid directive says otherwise, keep housemates safe, preserve the scene, and report immediately to the supervisor.
Direct the response, make notifications, secure records and property, and write or collect incident reports.
Support the response, give medical information to responders and physician, and take part in the mortality review.
Support housemates, coordinate with the ISC and guardian, gather the record, and complete discharge documentation.
Make reports to CIRAS, OIG and law enforcement as required, ensure guardian notification, convene the mortality review, and report to the governing body.
Review mortality review findings and approve corrective action through the QA plan.

documentation: Incident report and staff statements
Log of notifications with date, time and person reached
CIRAS report and confirmation
OIG and law enforcement reports, when made
Copy of the directive and EMS/coroner documents received
Inventory of personal property and funds with witness signatures
Mortality review report, corrective action plan and completion record
Staff training records on death response

policies.title: Record Confidentiality and Safekeeping
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors and governing body members who create, use, or have access to individuals' records, in paper or electronic form
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy of the people [AGENCY NAME] serves and to prevent the loss or destruction of their records.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(h)(1), which requires the CILA agency to ensure the confidentiality of individuals' records in accordance with the Act and to ensure safekeeping of all records against loss or destruction. [AGENCY NAME] follows the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110). Records and communications are disclosed only with valid consent or as the Act allows. All records are kept in locked storage or in access-controlled electronic systems. A copy of each release authorization is kept in the individual's record. Confidentiality training occurs at orientation. Individuals have the right to confidentiality as part of their rights under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250. To the extent [AGENCY NAME] is a covered entity or uses protected health information in ways covered by HIPAA, it also follows 45 CFR 164.530 (administrative requirements) as set out in RTS-05.

definitions.definition: The Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act, 740 ILCS 110, which governs the confidentiality of records and communications of individuals receiving developmental disability services.

Any paper or electronic information about an individual, including the cumulative case record, chronological record, Personal Plan, Implementation Strategy, MARs, incident reports, and billing files that identify an individual.
A written, signed, dated consent by the individual or guardian that states what may be released, to whom, for what purpose, and for how long.
Consent given voluntarily, without coercion, with understanding of the information, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Informed consent includes consent for releases of information.

procedures: Records custodian: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] names a records custodian in writing. The custodian is responsible for this policy, for the access list, and for reporting any loss or breach.

Paper storage: Paper records at the site are kept in a locked cabinet or room. Only staff on the access list hold the key or code. Records are returned to storage after use and are never left out on counters, in vehicles or in common areas.

Electronic systems: Electronic records are kept only in agency-approved systems with unique user log-ins, password rules, automatic log-off, and role-based access. Staff do not share log-ins. Staff do not store records on personal devices, personal email or personal cloud accounts.

Access list: The custodian maintains a written access list by job role. Direct support professionals see the information needed to give support. The QIDP, nurse and administrator see more. The custodian reviews the list quarterly and on any staff change, and removes access on the day of separation.

Orientation training: Before having access to any record, each new staff member, volunteer and contractor receives confidentiality training covering the Confidentiality Act and this policy. They sign a confidentiality statement that goes in the personnel file. Training is repeated annually (see TRN-04).
Need to know: Staff open or discuss records only when needed for their job. Staff do not discuss individuals in public places, on social media, or with people not involved in support.

Releases of information: Before releasing any information, staff check for a valid, signed, current authorization for release from the individual or guardian. The authorization names the recipient, purpose, content, and expiration. If it is not valid, the release does not happen. The administrator is consulted for requests that do not fit the form.
Copy of each authorization: The QIDP places a copy of every authorization in the individual's record, logs each release made under it (date, what was sent, to whom, by whom), and records revocations.

Explaining consent: The QIDP explains each release request to the individual in a way they understand, in their preferred communication mode, and supports the guardian in making an informed choice. Consent is never obtained by pressure.

Disclosures without consent: Staff do not decide on their own whether the Act allows a disclosure without consent, including to law enforcement or in response to a subpoena. They refer the request to the administrator, who verifies the legal basis before release and documents it.
Regulators and advocates: The administrator makes records available to BALC, DDD, OIG and other authorized monitors as the law allows, following REC-04 and GPR-09, and logs what was provided.

Sending information: Records are sent only by secure methods (encrypted email or portal, or sealed envelope with tracking). Fax or email is used only with a verified recipient. Mistaken disclosures are reported under step 14.
Transport: Records taken off site (for example to a physician) stay with a staff member in a closed container and are returned the same day.

Loss, theft or breach: Any staff member who discovers lost, stolen or misdirected records or unauthorized access tells the administrator immediately. The administrator investigates, recovers what can be recovered, notifies the individual or guardian, notifies others as required, and records corrective action. When applicable, this includes the process in RTS-05.

Protection from loss or destruction: The custodian makes sure electronic records are backed up on a regular schedule, stored securely, and tested for restore. Paper records are stored away from water, heat and fire risks. Fire-rated storage or scanned copies are used for permanent records when feasible.
Disposal: Records are destroyed only after the retention period in REC-04 ends, by shredding or secure wipe, and the destruction is logged with date, method and the person who did it.

Annual audit: The custodian audits a sample of records each year for storage, access, authorization copies and sign-in logs, and reports the results to the QA committee (QA-01). Corrective actions are tracked.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt this policy and receive annual audit results.
Name the records custodian, approve non-routine disclosures, and respond to breaches.
Keep the access list, maintain storage and security, track authorizations and conduct the annual audit.
Explain and obtain consents, file authorization copies and log releases.
Keep information confidential, use only what is needed, store records securely and report any loss or breach immediately.

documentation: Signed confidentiality statement for each staff member, volunteer and contractor
Access list and quarterly review record
Authorization for release forms and release log
Breach or loss incident reports and corrective actions
Record destruction log
Annual record audit report

policies.title: Chronological Record Standards and Electronic Signatures
policies.applies_to: All staff who write or sign entries in an individual's chronological record, and the staff who administer the electronic record system
policies.purpose: To make sure every entry in an individual's record is legible, dated, authenticated and correctable in a way that keeps the original visible, and to set the safeguards for electronic signatures.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(h)(2)(A)-(C) and 115.320(h)(5)(A)-(D). [AGENCY NAME] keeps a chronological record for each individual, accessible at the program site. Each entry is legible, dated, and authenticated by the signature and title of the person making it. Corrections are initialed and made so that the original incorrect entry stays legible. When symbols or abbreviations are used, the agency provides a legend that is standardized across the whole agency. The agency accepts electronic or computer-generated signature codes as authentication only under the safeguards in this policy: a unique identifier for each user through a confidential access code, written confidentiality and sole-user certifications, periodic monitoring with corrective action, a verification process, and separate authentication of each generated report.

definitions.definition: The dated, running record of services, observations, events and contacts for an individual, kept at the program site.
The signature and title (handwritten or electronic) of the person making an entry, showing who made it and confirming its content.
A unique identifier, generated through a confidential access code, that serves as the user's signature in the electronic record.
The agency-wide list of approved symbols and abbreviations and their meanings.
A user ID and confidential access code assigned to one person only.

procedures: Location: The chronological record for each individual is kept at the program site where the individual lives, in a place accessible to staff on duty and secured under REC-01. If the record is kept electronically, it is viewable at the site on a device staff can access during every shift.

Entry standard: Each entry states the date (and time when relevant), is written in clear, legible, factual language, and is signed with the full name or approved initials identifiable from a signature sheet, followed by the staff member's title. Paper entries are written in permanent blue or black ink.
No blanks or backdating: Staff do not leave blank lines between entries and do not backdate. A late entry is marked "late entry" with the current date and time and the date of the event it describes.

Corrections on paper: To correct an error, the writer draws a single line through the incorrect entry so it stays legible, writes the correct information, and initials and dates the correction. Staff never use correction fluid, tape, erasure or obliteration.

Legend: The QIDP maintains one agency-wide legend of symbols and abbreviations, approved by [ADMINISTRATOR NAME]. The legend is kept in the front of every paper record or accessible in the electronic system, and staff use only abbreviations on the legend. Changes apply to all sites on the same date and are taught to staff.

Signature sheet: Each staff member who writes in paper records signs a signature and initials sheet during orientation so that entries can be identified. The sheet is kept in the personnel file and updated.

Adoption of electronic signatures: The governing body, through this policy, permits authentication by electronic or computer-generated signature. Only system users approved by the administrator receive identifiers.
Unique identifiers: The system administrator issues each approved user a unique identifier generated through a confidential access code. No group, shared or generic log-ins are allowed.

Confidentiality certification: Before activation, each user signs a written certification that the identifier will be kept strictly confidential. The certification includes the agency's commitment to terminate use of any identifier that is misused.

Sole-user certification: Each user also signs a written certification that he or she is the only person with access to the identifier. Users do not lend, share or write down their codes where others may see them. Users change a code that may be known to someone else and report the suspected misuse to the administrator the same day.

Periodic monitoring: The system administrator reviews identifier use at least quarterly. The review looks at log-in times, shared or simultaneous log-ins, entries outside work shifts and active identifiers of separated staff. The administrator records findings and corrective action, such as retraining, code reset, or termination of the identifier.
Termination of identifiers: The system administrator disables an identifier on the user's last day, on reassignment that removes need for access, and immediately on confirmed misuse.
Required fields: The electronic system is set so designated fields must be completed before an entry can be saved or signed. The system administrator checks that this setting is in place.

Corrections in the electronic record: Errors are corrected only by a separate, subsequent authenticated entry that identifies the earlier entry, states the correction, and shows the date, time and author. The original entry cannot be deleted or overwritten.
User verification: After completing an entry or document, the user has an opportunity to review the content and signature and to confirm it before it is finalized.

Periodic sampling: At least quarterly, the QIDP or QA designee samples system-generated records for each site and checks them for accuracy against source information. Results and corrective actions are reported to the QA committee (QA-01).

Reports: Each report that a user generates from the system (for example, a progress report or a summary) is separately authenticated by that user with his or her signature and title or identifier before it is placed in the record or shared.

Training: Orientation and annual training cover documentation standards, the legend, correction rules and electronic signature safeguards (see TRN-03). Supervisors spot-check entries each month and coach staff on problems.

responsibilities.duty: Adopt the policy permitting electronic signatures and receive monitoring results through QA.
Approve system users and the legend, and ensure corrective action on monitoring findings.
Issue and terminate identifiers, hold signed certifications, configure required fields, and monitor use quarterly.
Maintain the legend, sample records, and coach staff on documentation.
Write accurate, legible, dated and signed entries, correct errors correctly, and protect their identifiers.

documentation: Chronological record for each individual
Agency-wide legend of symbols and abbreviations
Signature and initials sheets
Signed confidentiality certification and sole-user certification for each electronic user
Quarterly identifier monitoring log and corrective actions
Quarterly record sampling results
Training records on documentation

policies.title: Record Contents at Entry and During Service
policies.applies_to: QIDPs, nurses, site supervisors, direct support professionals and administrative staff who gather, file or update individuals' records
policies.purpose: To make sure each individual's record holds the information required at entry and throughout service, and that it is complete, current and available to the people who need it.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(h)(3)(A)-(H) (record contents at entry) and 115.320(h)(4)(A)-(F) (record contents during the period of service). On an individual's entry into [AGENCY NAME], the agency obtains, records and updates as necessary the information in Procedure 3. During the period of service, the agency enters in the individual's record the items listed in Procedure 6. All items are kept up to date. The current Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy are kept at the residence. Records are protected under REC-01 and authenticated under REC-02.

definitions.definition: The date an individual begins receiving CILA services from [AGENCY NAME].
The person-centered plan developed with the individual, guardian and Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency, which identifies the outcomes the individual wants and the supports needed.
The agency's plan, on Form IL462-4470, for how it will support the outcomes in the Personal Plan that the agency agreed to support, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 and 115.230.
The qualified intellectual disabilities professional responsible for the individual's plan, implementation, and monthly progress review.
A procedure that restricts a right or that requires special approval, such as a behavior intervention or rights restriction (see GPR-03 and RTS-02).

procedures: Record opened: Before or on the day of entry, the QIDP opens the individual's cumulative record. The record is kept per REC-01, and a chronological record is begun per REC-02.
Entry checklist: The QIDP uses the agency entry checklist so that no required item is missed. The administrator reviews the completed checklist within [NUMBER, e.g., 7] days of entry.

Information obtained at entry: The QIDP obtains, records and updates as necessary: (A) identifying information; (B) the court-appointed guardianship order, if applicable; (C) the name, address and telephone number of the legal guardian or emergency contact; (D) the language spoken or understood, including the preferred mode of communication; (E) prescribed medications, reactions and side effects, and allergies; (F) physical and dental examinations and medical history; (G) consent to receive emergency medical services; and (H) copies of the authorization for release of information.

Identifying and guardian information: The QIDP enters identifying information and the guardianship order, if any, and confirms guardian or emergency contact details by phone. If the individual has no guardian, the individual names an emergency contact and the QIDP documents it.

Communication and health: The QIDP records the individual's language and preferred communication mode (including any device or interpreter). The nurse records the medication list, reactions, side effects and allergies and obtains the physical and dental examinations and medical history from the individual's providers. Missing items are requested in writing, with follow-up documented.

During service the following are entered in the record: (A) written informed consent by the individual or guardian to participate in a CILA; (B) prior service history; (C) the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy (see 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230); (D) assessments and reassessments (see Section 115.225; verify the subsection against the official text); (E) documentation of approval to use special procedures and the results of their use; and (F) monthly documentation of progress toward Personal Plan outcomes, signed and dated by the QIDP.

Informed consent to participate: The QIDP explains CILA participation in the individual's communication mode and gets written informed consent from the individual or guardian, free of coercion, before or at entry. The consent is filed in the record.
Prior service history: The QIDP collects and files prior service history from the ISC, previous providers and the individual and guardian, and updates it when new information comes in.

Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy: The QIDP files the Personal Plan received from the ISC. Within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, the QIDP develops the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470, based on the Personal Plan and assessments, with the individual and guardian taking part. The individual or guardian signs it. The ISC does not sign or approve it. The individual and guardian get a copy of the strategy and of each update, and the ISC gets a copy. The current Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy are kept at the residence.
Assessments: The QIDP files each assessment and reassessment with its date and author, and tracks due dates on the record checklist.

Special procedures: Before any special procedure is used, the QIDP files documentation of the required approvals (see GPR-03, GPR-04 and RTS-02). After use, the staff who used it record the results, and the QIDP files them.

Monthly progress: At least monthly, the QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy, writes the progress documentation toward Personal Plan outcomes, and signs and dates it. The QIDP documents any needed changes and tells the individual, guardian and ISC.

Rights and related forms: The QIDP also files the signed Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) given at entry and annually, along with the GAC, OIG, Department and Equip for Equality contact information.

Keeping items current: The QIDP reviews each record monthly for missing, expired or outdated items and updates them. Changes in guardianship, medications, allergies, contacts or communication needs are entered on the day they are learned.
Record checks: The nurse checks medical items quarterly. The administrator audits a sample of records quarterly against the entry and service checklists and reports to QA (QA-01).

Access at the site: Staff on duty can reach the current medication list, allergies, emergency contacts, consent to emergency care and Implementation Strategy at the residence at all times, including overnight.
Correcting gaps: If an item is missing, the QIDP writes a dated note explaining why and the plan and date to get it. The QIDP does not backdate documents.

responsibilities.duty: Open the record, collect and file entry and service items, develop the Implementation Strategy, and complete monthly progress documentation.
Obtain and update medication, allergy, medical and dental information.
Keep the residence copy of the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy current and ensure staff can access emergency information.
Review entry checklists and audit records quarterly.
Take part in planning, give consents and receive copies of the Implementation Strategy and updates.

documentation: Entry checklist
Identifying information sheet and guardianship order
Guardian or emergency contact record
Communication profile
Medication, allergy, medical and dental records
Consent to emergency medical services
Authorizations for release of information
Written informed consent to participate in a CILA
Prior service history
Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy (Form IL462-4470) with signatures
Assessments and reassessments
Special procedure approvals and results
Monthly QIDP progress documentation
Quarterly record audit results

policies.title: Record Retention, Access and Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, records custodian, QIDP, nurse, and any staff who prepare, store, release or submit records or reports
policies.purpose: To make sure records are kept for the required period, are available to the State on request, and that every recurring report and filing to the State is submitted on time.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] retains records for the period in Procedure 1, makes records available to the Illinois Department of Human Services Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC) and the Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) on request, and keeps a calendar of recurring State report due dates. Required reports include CIRAS incidents, OIG reports, restraint reports, notice of ownership change to BALC and DDD within 60 business days, the renewal application at least 120 days before the license expires, and the annual rights-restriction and health-risk reviews. Records are kept confidential and safe under REC-01. Where EVV applies to the agency's claims, EVV compliance reports are also kept.

definitions.definition: The minimum length of time the agency must keep a record before it can be destroyed.
A report, notice, application or review that the agency must submit to or complete for the State on a stated schedule.
The agency's master list of recurring State filings and due dates, with the person responsible and completion dates.
The IDHS Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification, which licenses CILA agencies, inspects sites and conducts renewal and complaint surveys.

procedures: Retention period: No retention period was verified when this manual was written. Before adoption, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] confirms the retention period for individuals' records with BALC and DDD, and checks the waiver document, and records the answer here as [RETENTION PERIOD IN YEARS, confirmed with BALC/DDD on DATE]. The agency keeps records for the longer of that period or any longer period required by another law, contract or open audit, claim or legal matter. Documentation required by 45 CFR 164.530(j) (HIPAA policies and related documentation) is kept at least six years.

Retention schedule: The records custodian keeps a written retention schedule by record type (individual records, personnel records, financial and billing records, incident and investigation records, QA records, and fire drill and inspection records) with start date, retention period and destruction date.

Closed records: When an individual leaves, the QIDP completes the record and the custodian files it as a closed record in secure storage, marked with the closing date and the earliest destruction date. Closed records stay protected under REC-01 for the whole retention period.
Hold on destruction: The administrator places a hold on destruction of any record involved in an open investigation, complaint, audit, claim or lawsuit until written release from the administrator.

Access by BALC and DDD: The records custodian makes records available to BALC and DDD on request, at the site or by secure electronic means. Staff who receive a request notify [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] right away. Staff check the requester's identity and authority, and record what was provided, the date and who provided it.

Survey readiness: The custodian keeps the records needed for renewal and complaint surveys, including current Personal Plans and Implementation Strategies at each residence, in a standard order that surveyors can find easily.

Master reporting calendar: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] maintains the reporting calendar. It lists, at a minimum: CIRAS critical incident reports; reports to OIG; restraint reports; notice to BALC and DDD of any ownership change within 60 business days; the license renewal application, due at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice; annual rights-restriction reviews; annual health-risk reviews; and the recurring items in Procedure 8.

Other recurring items: The calendar also includes the annual review of the disaster preparedness plan, quarterly first aid kit checks, annual fire extinguisher inspection, fire and evacuation drills, annual criminal and registry checks (every 365 days), annual rights information to individuals, monthly QIDP reviews, Quality Assurance reviews, wage pass-through certifications, and, where EVV applies, quarterly EVV compliance.

Calendar controls: Each entry on the calendar shows the due date, the person responsible, a reminder date at least [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days before, the date completed, and where the proof is filed. The administrator reviews the calendar monthly.

Critical incident and OIG reports: When an event occurs, the staff member responsible reports under CI-01 and CI-02. The administrator keeps copies and confirmations in the incident file and checks them against the calendar each month.
Restraint reports: The administrator makes sure any report of restraint use is made as required under GPR-04 and is kept in the incident file and, where applicable, the individual's record.

Annual reviews: The QIDP schedules annual rights-restriction reviews (RTS-02) and the nurse schedules annual health-risk reviews (HLT-02) for each individual and files the dated results in the record. The administrator checks completion each month.
Ownership change: The administrator tells BALC and DDD in writing of any change in ownership within 60 business days and files the notice and proof of delivery.

License renewal: When the Department sends notice, the administrator starts the renewal packet and submits the application at least 120 days before expiration. The administrator keeps the proof of submission and the governing body is informed.

EVV: If DDD confirms that EVV applies to any of the agency's claims, the billing manager keeps the EVV compliance reports and tracks quarterly compliance against the 75% standard (see FIN-01). If applicability is unconfirmed, the administrator asks DDD in writing and keeps the reply.

Destruction: At the end of the retention period, and with no hold, the custodian gets the administrator's written approval, destroys the record by secure shredding or wiping, and logs what was destroyed, date, method and person.
Annual review: The administrator reviews the retention schedule and reporting calendar every year, and when rules change, and reports results to the QA committee (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Confirm the retention period, maintain the reporting calendar, authorize destruction and holds, and submit State filings.
Keep the retention schedule, store closed records securely, respond to access requests and log destruction.
Close records and schedule annual rights-restriction reviews.
Complete annual health-risk reviews.
Keep EVV compliance reports where applicable.
Receive reporting compliance results and be informed of renewal and ownership filings.

documentation: Retention schedule with confirmed retention period and confirmation correspondence
Closed record log
Destruction holds and destruction log
Log of access requests from BALC and DDD
Master State reporting calendar with proof of submission
CIRAS, OIG and restraint report copies and confirmations
Ownership change notice and renewal application with proof of delivery
Annual rights-restriction and health-risk review records
EVV compliance reports, where applicable

policies.title: Department Contractual and Financial Requirements, Medicaid Billing and Documentation, EVV and Wage Pass-Through
policies.applies_to: Administrator, billing and finance staff, QIDPs, site supervisors and direct support professionals whose documentation supports billing
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] meets its contractual and financial obligations to the Department, bills Medicaid accurately only for services that were authorized and delivered, and passes wage increases through to direct care staff.
policies.policy: This policy meets 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320(i) (Financial and operational requirements): [AGENCY NAME] complies with Department rules regulating its contractual and financial relationship with the Department. CILA services are paid under the Medicaid Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04), for which the Department of Healthcare and Family Services (HFS) is the Medicaid agency and the IDHS Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) is the operating agency. The agency bills only for services identified in the Personal Plan, and tells the Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency if a service change is needed. Enrollment and billing run through IMPACT, and enrollment must be complete before federal reimbursement. Where EVV applies, the agency keeps quarterly compliance above 75% from April 1, 2026. Whether EVV applies to 60D/61H CILA claims has not been verified, so the agency confirms this with DDD in writing. The agency certifies to DDD that wage increases are passed through to direct care staff. The agency also complies with the HCBS settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c).

definitions.definition: The Illinois Medicaid Program Advanced Cloud Technology system used for Medicaid provider enrollment and reimbursement.
The person-centered plan that identifies the services and supports an individual receives; services billed must be identified in it.
A system that electronically verifies the date, time, location, service and worker for certain visits, for providers billing services covered by the DDD EVV policy.
The requirement that wage and rate increases the State funds be paid to direct care staff, with certification to DDD.
Service codes for CILA claims; confirm with DDD which codes the EVV requirement covers.

procedures: Responsible person: [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] names a billing manager in writing and keeps a current list of the Department's contracts, rules, notices and policies that apply to the agency's financial relationship with the Department.

IMPACT enrollment: Before billing any Medicaid claim, the billing manager completes IMPACT enrollment, confirms the enrollment is active, and files the confirmation. The agency does not bill until enrollment is complete and the license and provider agreement are in place (see FIN-02).

Keeping enrollment current: The billing manager updates IMPACT when ownership, address, contacts, bank information or license status changes, and tracks required revalidations on the reporting calendar (REC-04).

Authorization check: Before each billing period, the billing manager confirms for each individual the current approved services, rate and dates in the Department's records. The agency does not bill outside the authorized dates or amounts.

Services identified in the Personal Plan: The QIDP confirms that every service billed is identified in the individual's Personal Plan. If a needed service is not in the plan, or the individual's needs change, the QIDP tells the ISC in writing as soon as the need is known and documents the notice. The agency does not bill for the service until the plan and authorization are updated.

Implementation Strategy: The QIDP makes sure the Implementation Strategy is completed within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, signed by the individual or guardian (the ISC does not sign or approve it), and shared with the individual, guardian and ISC.

Rate packets: When a rate determination packet or a request for additional supports is needed, the QIDP prepares it with the ISC under PCS-02. The billing manager does not bill at a changed rate until the Department confirms it.

Documentation supports billing: Direct support professionals record daily service documentation under PCS-03 and REC-02. The Site Supervisor reviews each day's documentation before the end of the next business day for completeness, signatures and attendance entries.

Pre-billing review: Before submitting claims, the billing manager reconciles attendance and census (admissions, discharges, hospital stays and leave days) with daily documentation and authorizations, and resolves differences. The administrator approves the claim batch.

Claim submission: The billing manager submits claims through IMPACT within the Department's billing deadlines, keeps remittance advices, and reconciles payments within [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days. Rejected or underpaid claims are corrected and resubmitted promptly.

Overpayments: If the agency finds it was paid for a service it did not deliver or was not authorized to bill, the administrator reports and returns the overpayment as the Department directs, documents the cause and fixes the process. The agency does not keep known overpayments.

EVV applicability: The administrator asks DDD in writing whether EVV applies to the agency's CILA claims, including 60D and 61H. The agency files the reply. If EVV applies, the billing manager completes EVV setup, staff training and system integration before the compliance date.

EVV compliance (where it applies): From April 1, 2026, the billing manager tracks EVV compliance each month and keeps quarterly compliance above 75%. Staff clock in and out as trained, missing or manual entries are corrected with documented reasons, and results are reported to the administrator monthly and to the QA committee quarterly (QA-01). If compliance falls below standard, the administrator sets a corrective action plan within [NUMBER, e.g., 10] business days.

Wage pass-through: When the State funds a wage or rate increase for direct care staff, such as the January 1, 2024 wage/rate increase, the administrator makes sure the increase is paid to direct care staff in the amounts required, effective on the dates required, and shown in payroll records.

Wage pass-through certification: The administrator certifies to DDD that wage increases have been passed through to direct care staff, by the deadline in the Department's notice, with payroll records supporting the certification. The billing manager keeps the certification and payroll back-up.

Financial and contract compliance: The administrator reads each Department notice, contract or rule change on receipt, assigns an owner and due date, and updates this policy and the reporting calendar. The agency submits financial, cost and other reports the Department requires by their due dates.

Fraud prevention: Staff never record services not given, change documentation to support billing, or bill for another person's services. Staff report suspected billing errors or fraud to the administrator. The agency does not retaliate against anyone who reports in good faith. Any report that the administrator believes involves a possible violation of law is handled as required by law.
Individuals' funds separate from agency funds: Individuals' personal funds and room-and-board funds are kept separate from the agency's operating funds and handled under FIN-03.

Audit and review: The billing manager samples claims quarterly against authorizations and documentation. The administrator reports results, errors and corrective action to the governing body and the QA committee at least annually.

Records and retention: Billing records, authorizations, remittances, EVV reports, wage certifications and payroll back-up are kept for the period in REC-04 and made available to the Department, HFS and other authorized reviewers.

responsibilities.duty: Oversee the agency's financial and contractual compliance and receive annual audit results.
Ensure compliance with Department rules, approve claim batches, confirm EVV applicability with DDD, and sign wage pass-through certifications.
Keep IMPACT enrollment, reconcile authorizations and documentation, submit and reconcile claims, and track EVV and overpayments.
Confirm billed services are in the Personal Plan, notify the ISC of needed service changes and complete the Implementation Strategy.

responsibilities.role: Site Supervisor and direct support professionals
responsibilities.duty: Provide services as planned and document them accurately and on time; use EVV as trained where it applies.

documentation: IMPACT enrollment confirmation and updates
Authorization and rate records
Notices to the ISC about service changes
Daily service documentation and attendance and census records
Claim batch approvals, claims and remittance advices
Overpayment records and returns
Written EVV applicability inquiry and DDD reply
EVV compliance reports and corrective action plans, where applicable
Wage pass-through certification and payroll back-up
Quarterly claim audit results

policies.title: Licensure, Certification and Provider Agreements
policies.applies_to: Governing body, Administrator, QIDP, and all staff involved in licensure, enrollment and renewal activities
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] holds and keeps a valid IDHS Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification (BALC) license, enrolls correctly as a Medicaid waiver provider, and meets every licensure, renewal and notification deadline under 210 ILCS 135 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates as a Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) agency only under a current BALC license. Under 210 ILCS 135, a CILA is a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision, and [AGENCY NAME] will not exceed that number at any site. The agency completes the BALC license first and then enrolls with the Division of Developmental Disabilities (DDD) through IMPACT. It does not bill the Medicaid HCBS Waiver for Adults with Developmental Disabilities (IL.0350.R05.04) until both steps are complete. Under the waiver, HFS is the Medicaid agency and IDHS-DDD is the operating agency. The agency tracks and meets all deadlines, including completing new-provider requirements within one year of requesting an application, becoming operational within 18 months, filing renewal at least 120 days before expiration after Department notice, and notifying BALC and DDD of any ownership change within 60 business days. This policy supports the application requirements of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.410, which include the agency's policies and procedures, organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications.

definitions.definition: The IDHS Bureau of Accreditation, Licensure and Certification, which issues provisional and permanent CILA agency licenses, inspects sites and conducts renewal and complaint surveys.
A Community Integrated Living Arrangement: a site where 8 or fewer individuals with a developmental disability live under agency supervision (210 ILCS 135; 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120).
The initial license, valid for up to one year, covering one site serving up to 8 individuals, issued before the BALC site visit that leads to a permanent license.
The Illinois Medicaid provider enrollment system through which the agency completes DDD/HFS enrollment steps after BALC licensure.
The person designated in writing by the governing body to act for [AGENCY NAME] in dealings with BALC, DDD and HFS.

procedures: The governing body designates [ADMINISTRATOR NAME] as the authorized CILA agency representative in a written resolution kept in the governing body minutes.

When the agency requests a BALC application, the Administrator records the request date and starts a licensure tracking calendar. The calendar shows the one-year deadline to complete new-provider requirements and the 18-month deadline to be operational.

The Administrator assembles the application package: the completed application, the nonrefundable application fee (not to exceed $200 under 210 ILCS 135/4), the agency's policies and procedures, the organizational chart, staffing patterns and staff qualifications. A second person checks the package against the BALC checklist before submission.

The Administrator confirms that the certifications in the application are accurate. They cover compliance with Section 4 of the Act, the Confidentiality Act, 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115 and 120, and 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(4), and they state that provider-owned or controlled sites meet 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E). The governing body chair or Administrator signs only after this check.

The Administrator arranges electronic fingerprint background checks for owners, authorized representatives, officers and the administrator as BALC and IDPH require, and files the results in the licensure file.

The Administrator confirms that the site meets the one-site, 8-or-fewer limit and that fire clearance is requested through BALC and the Office of the State Fire Marshal when the property is ready. The agency supplies all fire clearances and documents BALC requests so the site inspection can be scheduled (BALC runs it within 15 working days after clearances and other documents are received).

The agency does not admit any individual until BALC has issued the provisional license. The Administrator posts the license where the agency's licensing documents are kept and keeps a copy at the certified site.

After licensure, the Administrator completes DDD and IMPACT enrollment steps and records the date each step is completed. No Medicaid claim is submitted until enrollment is confirmed in writing (see FIN-01).

The Administrator logs the date of the first admission and calendars the BALC site visit, which is due within six months of that admission. An unannounced BALC visit may occur at any time within the first year of the first admission, so the agency stays survey-ready at all times.

Before the site visit, the Administrator and QIDP run a mock review of the site, personnel files, training records and individual records against 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115. Findings are corrected and documented before BALC arrives.
When BALC issues deficiencies, the Administrator follows QA-02 and submits the plan of correction by the date BALC sets. The agency keeps the correction evidence in the licensure file.

Passing the site visit converts the provisional license to a permanent license. The Administrator records the license term shown on the document (in effect, three years) and calendars the expiration date.

On the Department's renewal notice, the Administrator files the renewal application at least 120 days before the license expires and keeps proof of filing. If no notice arrives, the Administrator contacts BALC at 312-814-5310 at least 150 days before expiration to confirm the renewal process. The 150-day contact point is an internal safeguard, not a rule requirement.
Before any change of ownership, the governing body notifies the Administrator. The Administrator notifies BALC and DDD in writing within 60 business days of the change and keeps the confirmation.

The Administrator reports any change that affects licensure or the provider agreement (administrator, site address, capacity, governing body composition) to BALC and DDD as they require, and updates the organizational chart (GOV-03).
The Administrator keeps all provider agreements, enrollment confirmations and rate documentation in the licensure file and reviews them with the governing body at least annually.

If a licensure deadline is at risk, the Administrator tells the governing body chair at once. The governing body decides the corrective action at its next meeting, or sooner if needed, and records it in the minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes the license application, designates the authorized representative, and reviews licensure status and deadlines at least annually.
Prepares and files all applications and renewals, keeps the licensure calendar, communicates with BALC, DDD and HFS, and reports ownership and other changes on time.
Helps prepare for BALC visits and supplies individual record evidence and Provider Support Team documentation.
Tracks deficiencies and plans of correction through QA-02 and reports status to the governing body.

documentation: Licensure file: application, fee receipt, certifications, correspondence with BALC, DDD and HFS
Licensure tracking calendar (one-year new-provider deadline, 18-month operational deadline, six-month site visit, renewal and expiration dates)
Provisional and permanent license copies and BALC inspection reports
IMPACT and DDD enrollment confirmations and provider agreements
Written notices of ownership or other changes to BALC and DDD, with proof of delivery
Governing body resolutions and minutes related to licensure

policies.title: Personal Funds and Property Management
policies.applies_to: Administrator, QIDP, direct support professionals, business/accounting staff, and any staff who handle an individual's money or belongings
policies.purpose: To protect each individual's money and property and to support each individual's control of their own personal resources, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200 and the HCBS settings requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4) require.
policies.policy: Individuals served by [AGENCY NAME] control their own personal resources. The agency supports each person to manage as much of their own money as the person can, with only the help and safeguards the person's Personal Plan calls for. Individual funds are never mixed with agency funds. Each person's funds are kept in a separate account, with a ledger, receipts for every transaction and a monthly reconciliation. Any charge to an individual for room and board is made only under a written agreement, and the agency verifies the permitted amount with DDD or BALC before setting it. Staff may never borrow from, lend to, or take anything of value from an individual. Suspected misuse of an individual's funds or property is reported as financial exploitation under GPR-05.

definitions.definition: All money belonging to an individual, including wages, benefits, allowances, gifts and any account in the individual's name, whether held by the individual, the agency or another party.
Items that belong to the individual, including clothing, furniture, electronics, jewelry, keepsakes and assistive devices.
Using an individual's money or property for anyone's benefit other than the individual's, or without the individual's informed consent. It is handled under GPR-05.
A written agreement between the individual (or guardian) and the agency that states what is charged for housing and food, and how the individual is told of any change.

procedures: At entry, the QIDP asks each individual and any guardian how the person wants to manage money. The QIDP assesses what help, if any, the person needs and records the result in the Personal Plan. Any limit on the person's access to or control of their money is handled as a rights restriction under RTS-02.
The Administrator designates the staff members who may assist with funds and keeps a current list. Only those staff, after training on this policy, may handle an individual's money.

For funds the agency holds at the individual's or guardian's request, the agency opens a separate account in each person's name (or the account type the funding source requires). Agency operating accounts are never used, and no person's funds are combined with another's or with agency funds.

The agency obtains written authorization from the individual or guardian before holding funds. The authorization states what the agency will hold, who may make deposits and withdrawals, and how the individual may access the money.
Each individual has full, prompt access to their own money during reasonable hours and for any lawful purpose. Staff may not require a reason, delay access, or condition access on behavior.

Staff keep a ledger for each individual showing the date, amount, purpose, balance, and the signatures of the staff member and the individual (or the reason the individual did not sign). Staff get a receipt for every purchase and attach it to the ledger.

Cash held in the home is limited to the amount the individual wants kept there and is stored in a locked place the individual can reach on request. Staff count it with the individual or a second staff member at each shift change if the agency is holding it.

The business office staff member reconciles each individual's ledger to the bank statement every month. A second person, who does not handle the individual's funds, reviews and signs the reconciliation within 30 days of the statement date.

Reconciliation errors or missing funds are reported to the Administrator the same day they are found and are investigated. Suspected theft or misuse is reported as financial exploitation under GPR-05 and CI-02, and the agency repays any loss it caused.

The agency gives each individual and guardian a statement of account at least quarterly and any time the individual or guardian asks. The statement is in a format the person can understand (see RTS-04).

Before charging room and board, the Administrator checks the permitted amount and any funding rules with DDD or BALC and records the response. The agency then signs a written agreement with the individual or guardian before any charge is made. Changes to the charge need written notice to the individual and guardian before the change takes effect.

The agency never charges an individual for items or services that its waiver rate pays for. It never requires an individual to give up benefits, wages or possessions to the agency as a condition of services.

At entry, a DSP and the individual, with the guardian if there is one, complete a written inventory of the individual's personal property. The inventory is updated when items are acquired, lost or disposed of, and at least annually. The individual signs it, or the reason the individual did not sign is noted.
Staff replace or reimburse any individual's property lost or damaged through agency negligence. The Administrator reviews each incident.

The individual's benefits and any representative payee arrangements are recorded in the record. If the agency serves as representative payee, it follows all Social Security Administration requirements. This is a separate role from room and board and from holding personal funds.

At discharge, the agency returns all funds and property to the individual or guardian within the time the individual's rights and applicable law require. It provides a final accounting and obtains a signed receipt.
The Administrator audits a sample of ledgers, receipts and reconciliations at least quarterly and reports results to the Quality Assurance committee (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures funds are segregated, reconciliations are completed, room and board agreements are in place, and audits and corrections are done.
Assesses each person's money management wishes and needs, writes them into the Personal Plan, and ensures any limits follow RTS-02.
Maintain ledgers and receipts, support the individual's access to money and property, and report any concern or discrepancy immediately.
Keep separate accounts, perform monthly reconciliations, and produce statements.
Never borrow, lend, take gifts of value, or use an individual's funds or property, and report suspected misuse under GPR-05.

documentation: Individual authorization to hold funds and Personal Plan section on money management
Individual ledgers with receipts
Monthly bank reconciliations with reviewer signatures
Quarterly statements of account
Room and board written agreement and notices of any change, plus the Administrator's written verification of permitted amounts
Personal property inventory
Incident, investigation and reimbursement records for any loss
Quarterly audit reports

policies.title: Individual Rights and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers, contractors, the Administrator, the QIDP, and the governing body
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual knows their rights, can use them, and lives in a setting that meets the Illinois CILA rule on individual rights and the federal HCBS settings requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects the rights of every individual under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250 and Chapter II of the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Code (405 ILCS 5), except that seclusion is not permitted. The agency gives and explains the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) at entry and again every year. The agency also tells each individual about the right to remain in the CILA unless the person voluntarily withdraws or meets the termination criteria. Individuals may contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of the Inspector General (OIG), the Department, and the agency's human rights committee, and staff help them do so. Individuals may choose their own private physicians and professionals, and the choice is recorded in the plan. All provider-owned or controlled sites meet 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E) and are not of a type described in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(5)(v), as required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200 and 115.410.

definitions.definition: The Department's current form that lists the rights of individuals receiving CILA services. The agency explains it at entry and annually.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: pressure or force used to make an individual do, or not do, something against the person's own wishes.
The federal requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)-(5) that home and community-based settings support integration, choice, privacy, dignity, and control over daily life.
A residence that the agency owns, leases or otherwise controls, where the added protections of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E) apply.

procedures: At or before entry, the QIDP gives each individual and guardian the current Rights of Individuals form (IL 462-1201) and explains it in plain language and the person's preferred communication mode (see RTS-04). The QIDP asks the person to state what they understood and answers questions.

The QIDP records the date, the person who explained the rights, the communication method used, and the individual's or guardian's signature or acknowledgment in the record. If the individual declines to sign, staff note that.

The QIDP repeats the explanation every year, at or before the annual Personal Plan meeting, and any time the form is revised. The agency checks the Department's website each quarter to confirm it is using the current version of IL 462-1201.

At entry and annually, staff give each individual, in an accessible format, the address and telephone number of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's OIG, the Department, and the agency's human rights committee ([PHONE] for the agency's own contact). A current contact sheet is posted where individuals can see it and kept in each person's room or personal folder if they choose.

Staff offer to help individuals contact any of these resources, including making a call, writing a letter or setting up a meeting, and the individual is not required to tell staff why they are contacting them. Staff never read, block or retaliate over such contact.

The agency tells each individual that they have the right to remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the termination criteria in PCS-05, and that no one may discharge them for any other reason.

The agency supports each individual's right to be free from abuse, neglect, exploitation, coercion and restraint, and to use the complaint process in GPR-06. Seclusion is never used. Time-out and aversive procedures are never used (see GPR-04).

The QIDP asks each person which physicians and other professionals they want to use, and records private provider choices in the Personal Plan. Staff arrange appointments and transportation to that provider as the person wishes.
The agency does not place any condition on rights that is not in an approved, documented rights modification. Any restriction follows RTS-02.

The Administrator and QIDP check each provider-owned or controlled site against 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E) before the first admission and at least annually. The review confirms that: (A) each individual has a legally enforceable agreement giving protections like a tenant's, or a comparable written agreement; (B) each person has privacy in their sleeping and living space, including lockable doors and choice of roommates; (C) people can furnish and decorate their space, control their daily schedule and activities, and have access to food at any time; (D) people can have visitors at any time; and (E) the setting is physically accessible.

The Administrator confirms that no site is, and no practice has the effect of, a setting of a type described in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(5)(v), including isolation from the broader community. The review records community access, employment and activity choices (see PCS-04).

Staff do not use house rules that limit rights, such as set visiting hours, set bedtimes, locked kitchens or limits on phone or internet use, unless an approved modification under RTS-02 permits them for a specific person.

The QIDP records each person's choices about roommates, room furnishing, daily schedule, meals, visitors and community activities in the Personal Plan and ensures staff schedules follow those choices.

Staff report any suspected violation of a person's rights to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator reviews it, takes corrective action, and, if abuse, neglect, exploitation or coercion is suspected, reports it under GPR-05.
The Human Rights Committee reviews rights issues and any complaints as GPR-02 requires, and its findings go to the governing body (GOV-02).
All staff are trained on individual rights and the HCBS settings requirements at orientation and every year (TRN-04).
The Administrator reports rights concerns and site review results to the Quality Assurance committee at least quarterly (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures rights materials are current, the annual site review is completed, and violations are corrected and reported.
Explains the rights form at entry and annually, records the explanation, records provider and lifestyle choices in the Personal Plan, and arranges contact with outside advocates.
Respect each person's rights daily, help individuals reach advocacy organizations, and report any concern at once.
Reviews rights matters and complaints as GPR-02 requires.
Reviews rights and settings compliance reports and supports corrective action.

documentation: Signed or acknowledged IL 462-1201 at entry and each year, with date, explainer and communication method
Contact sheet for GAC, Equip for Equality, OIG, the Department and the agency's human rights committee, and record of its distribution
Personal Plan entries for provider choice, roommate choice, schedule and visitor preferences
Annual site review checklist for 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(A)-(E)
Residency or occupancy agreements
Records of rights concerns, corrective actions and reports
Staff training records on rights

policies.title: Rights Restrictions and Due Process
policies.applies_to: Administrator, QIDP, Provider Support Team, Human Rights Committee, Behavior Management Committee and all direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure no individual's rights are limited except through a documented, individualized, time-limited and reviewed modification, and that every individual can challenge a restriction and knows how.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not restrict any individual's rights except through a modification documented in that person's Personal Plan, based on a specific assessed need, as 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi)(F) requires. The record must show the less intrusive methods tried, a time limit, a data-based review, and informed consent from the individual or guardian. The Human Rights Committee reviews restrictions affecting a specific individual at least every six months (GPR-02). Restraint is allowed only under the conditions of 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245, and prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Seclusion, time-out and aversive procedures are never used (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250). The agency tells the individual and guardian how to appeal and whom to contact, including the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission (GAC), Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of the Inspector General (OIG) and the Department (DHS). The agency also follows the process for complaints required by 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320.

definitions.definition: Any limit on an individual's rights or on the HCBS settings protections in 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(vi), such as limits on access to food, visitors, money, or personal belongings, that is not required of all individuals in the setting and is supported by a specific assessed need.
A positive or supportive approach that does not limit rights, tried and documented before any restriction is considered.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120. Prone, supine and mechanical restraint are prohibited. Other restraint is allowed only if every condition in 115.245 is met.
A procedure defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 that uses pain, discomfort, loss of dignity or deprivation to change behavior. It is prohibited.

As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: agreement given voluntarily after the individual or guardian has been told, in understandable terms, what is proposed, why, the risks and the alternatives (see RTS-03).

procedures: Staff may not impose a rule, limit, or restriction on any individual unless it is an approved modification in that person's Personal Plan. Any staff member who sees a limit being applied without approval reports it to the Administrator the same day.

If a Provider Support Team member believes a restriction may be needed, the QIDP convenes the team and the individual (and guardian) to identify the specific, assessed need the restriction would address and to describe the behavior or condition in a written assessment.

The team documents the positive interventions and less intrusive methods already tried, with dates and results. A restriction cannot proceed until the record shows these methods were tried and did not work, or why they would not be safe.

The QIDP writes the proposed modification in the Personal Plan. It states the specific need, the exact restriction, how it will be carried out, and how it is proportionate to the need. It also gives the data that will be collected to measure its effect, a time limit, and the date of the first review.

The QIDP explains the proposed modification in plain language and the person's preferred communication mode. The individual and guardian are told they may refuse, ask questions, bring an advocate, and contact the outside organizations listed in this policy.

The agency obtains written informed consent from the individual or, where there is a guardian with authority, from the guardian, before the modification starts. The individual's own views are recorded even when a guardian consents. No restriction starts without consent. The record also states that the modification will not cause harm to the individual.

The Human Rights Committee reviews each proposed modification before it starts if it affects a specific individual's rights, and again at least every six months as GPR-02 requires. The committee's decision, date and any conditions are recorded. Behavior-related restrictions also go to the Behavior Management Committee (GPR-03).

For any restraint, the agency applies 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245 in full. There must be an immediate threat of serious physical harm and less restrictive measures proven ineffective. Restraint must be a modification in the Personal Plan approved by the individual or guardian and the Provider Support Team, and it must be in the behavior strategy. It also needs committee approval, a plan to reduce and eliminate it, staff trained in the specific restraint, and documentation that there is no medical or psychological contraindication. Prone, supine or mechanical restraint is never used, and any use is reported in CIRAS and to OIG (CI-02). See GPR-04.
Staff collect the data the modification requires every time it is applied and record it in the daily documentation (PCS-03). They do not apply the restriction beyond what the plan states.

The QIDP reviews the data with the team at each review date and decides whether to continue, change or end the modification. A modification ends on its time limit unless the team, the individual or guardian and the committee renew it after a new review. The QIDP records each decision.
The agency removes any restriction as soon as the assessed need ends and restores the right in full. Staff do not carry a restriction forward by habit or convenience.

At entry, annually, and whenever a restriction is proposed, the QIDP tells the individual and guardian how to object or appeal: first to the QIDP and Administrator under GPR-06, then to the Human Rights Committee, and at any time to GAC, Equip for Equality, OIG and the Department. The QIDP gives them each organization's address and telephone number.

The Administrator answers a written objection or appeal within the time frame stated in GPR-06 and records the outcome. The individual keeps the right to contact outside organizations whatever the outcome.
The agency never uses a restriction as punishment, for staff convenience, or because of a staffing shortage. It never uses seclusion, time-out or aversive procedures.

Staff who take part in a restraint that is not in the individual's Personal Plan report it immediately as a critical incident (CI-01), and the agency may require remediation training for them as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.245 allows.
The Administrator tracks all active modifications in a log showing person, restriction, start date, review dates and expiry. The log is given to the Quality Assurance committee quarterly (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures no unapproved restrictions are used, keeps the modification log, and answers appeals.
Leads the team assessment, writes the modification, obtains informed consent, schedules reviews, and informs the individual and guardian of appeal rights.
Identifies need, tries less intrusive methods, reviews data, and approves, changes or ends modifications.
Reviews restrictions affecting a specific individual before they start and at least every six months.
Apply only approved modifications as written, collect the required data, and report any unapproved restriction.

documentation: Personal Plan modification page: assessed need, less intrusive methods tried, restriction, time limit, data plan, review date
Written informed consent from the individual or guardian
Human Rights Committee and Behavior Management Committee review records
Data collected each time the restriction is used
Review decisions (continue, change, end)
Record that appeal rights and outside contacts were given
Modification log
Critical incident and CIRAS/OIG reports for any restraint

policies.title: Informed Consent, Decision-Making Support and Sexual Health
policies.applies_to: Administrator, QIDP, Provider Support Team, nurse, direct support professionals, and anyone who seeks consent or releases information
policies.purpose: To ensure that every consent is informed and voluntary, that individuals get the support they need to make their own decisions, and that the right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation is protected.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] obtains and documents the individual's informed consent to participate in a CILA, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200 requires. Informed consent also covers release of information. The agency presents every consent request in plain language and in the individual's preferred communication mode, and it supports the individual to make their own decisions. Where a guardian has legal authority, the agency documents that authority in the record, and a guardian's decisions never override an individual's rights beyond the scope of the court order.
