The Provider Support Team supports the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation, including a decision-making capacity assessment for consent to sexual activity, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220 requires. The agency follows 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320 on allegations of abuse, neglect and exploitation, including notification of a guardian or parent within 24 hours.

definitions.definition: As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: agreement given voluntarily by the individual or guardian after being told, in understandable terms, what is proposed, the reasons, risks, benefits and alternatives, and that consent may be refused or withdrawn.
As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: pressure, threat or inducement used to make a person act against their own wishes. Consent obtained through coercion is not valid.
A documented assessment by qualified Provider Support Team members of whether an individual understands and can decide about a specific matter, such as consent to sexual activity.
A person or entity appointed by a court with legal authority to make specific decisions for an individual. The authority is limited to what the order says.
Written permission from the individual or guardian for the agency to share specific information with a named person or organization (see RTS-05).

procedures: Before entry, the QIDP meets with the individual and, where there is one, the guardian. The QIDP explains the CILA services, the individual's rights, the house, the roommates, the costs and the right to leave, in plain language and in the person's preferred communication mode.

The QIDP checks that the person understands by asking them to say it in their own words, using pictures, demonstrations or other supports, and gives the person time to decide. The QIDP does not pressure the person or promise or threaten anything.

The individual (and guardian where applicable) signs the informed consent to participate in the CILA. The QIDP files it in the record at entry (REC-03). If the person cannot sign, the QIDP records how consent was shown and who witnessed it.

The agency obtains separate informed consent for each release of information, naming the recipient, the information, the purpose and an end date, and explains that the person may refuse or withdraw it. Staff release nothing without a valid consent, except where law requires or allows it (RTS-05).

For every other consent request (treatment, medication, photos, rights modifications, research, behavior supports), the person who asks for consent follows the same steps: plain-language explanation, preferred communication mode, time to decide, and a documented answer.

The QIDP verifies guardianship status at entry by obtaining a copy of the court order. The QIDP records the guardian's name, contact information and the scope of authority (person, estate, limited or plenary) in the record, and shares the scope with the team.

Where a guardian decides a matter, staff still ask for and record the individual's own preferences and give them effect where the order allows. Staff never apply a guardian's wishes to a matter outside the order.

The Provider Support Team supports decision-making through teaching, practice, visual aids, trusted people and time. The QIDP records each support in the Personal Plan so that a person's capacity is not assumed to be absent because of diagnosis.

The team respects the individual's right to sexual health and freedom from sexual exploitation. Staff discuss relationships, privacy, consent, safer sex and reproductive health respectfully and without judgment. They provide age-appropriate, accessible information and refer to health professionals when requested.

When an individual wants to engage in sexual activity and there is a question about whether the person can consent, the QIDP convenes the team to complete a decision-making capacity assessment. A qualified professional takes part. The assessment looks at whether the person understands the nature of the activity, the risks, the right to say no and the ability to recognize exploitation.

The team records the assessment, the supports offered (education, accessible information, counseling) and the outcome in the record. The person's privacy is protected, and results are shared only with those who need to know.

If the assessment shows the individual needs more support, the team provides it and reassesses later. The agency does not impose a blanket ban on relationships or sexual activity. Any limit on this right is a rights modification under RTS-02.

Staff protect individuals from sexual exploitation. Any suspected sexual abuse, coercion or exploitation is reported immediately under GPR-05, and CI-02 applies for law enforcement and OIG reports. The agency notifies the guardian or parent within 24 hours of receiving the allegation.
Staff never take part in sexual contact with an individual, and they follow STF-06 on professional boundaries.
The QIDP reviews consents at each annual Personal Plan meeting and whenever circumstances change, and updates or renews any consent that has expired or no longer matches the person's wishes.
All staff are trained on informed consent, coercion, decision-making support, guardianship scope and sexual health supports at orientation and every year (TRN-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures consent practices and guardian documentation are in place and that sexual exploitation allegations are reported.
Obtains and records informed consent, verifies guardianship, convenes capacity assessments, and reviews consents annually.
Supports decision-making, completes capacity assessments, and provides sexual health education and referrals.
Present information accessibly, respect decisions, protect privacy, and report suspected exploitation immediately.

documentation: Signed informed consent to participate in the CILA
Release-of-information consents with recipient, purpose and end date
Guardianship order copy and scope-of-authority summary
Personal Plan notes on decision-making supports and communication mode
Decision-making capacity assessments and team notes (restricted access)
Consents for treatment, medication and rights modifications
Reports and notifications of any suspected exploitation, with the 24-hour guardian notification
Training records

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Communication Access
policies.applies_to: All staff, volunteers and contractors; Administrator; QIDP; Provider Support Team
policies.purpose: To make sure no individual is treated differently or denied services because of a protected characteristic, and that every individual can understand and be understood through the communication supports they need.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not discriminate in admission, services, supports, discipline or discharge. The nondiscrimination categories are those in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320 and are set out in GPR-07. No otherwise qualified individual is denied placement solely because of diagnosis, and lack of agency capacity for a particular disability does not make a person ineligible (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.210). The agency complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101 et seq.), Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d) and Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act (29 USC 794). It provides interpreters, translated materials and assistive communication supports at no cost to the individual or guardian. Communal areas meet ADA accessibility standards (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200). The agency records each individual's preferred communication mode in the entry record.

definitions.definition: The way a person understands and expresses themselves best, such as spoken words, sign language, a communication device, pictures, writing, gestures or a trusted person's help.
A person's need for language help because English is not their primary language or they do not speak, read or understand it well.
Supports that make communication effective, including qualified interpreters, captioning, braille or large print, plain-language and picture formats, and assistive technology.
A change to a policy, practice, building or service that lets a person with a disability take part equally, unless it would cause an undue burden or fundamentally alter the service.

procedures: The Administrator posts a nondiscrimination notice at the agency office and gives it to each individual and guardian at entry. The notice states the agency's nondiscrimination commitments and how to file a complaint under GPR-06 or with outside agencies.

At intake and admission review, the Administrator and QIDP apply the nondiscrimination categories in GPR-07. They never deny or delay placement based on diagnosis, level of disability, behavior history alone, or the agency's lack of experience with a particular disability. If more training or support is needed, the agency plans for it (see GPR-07 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.210).

At entry, the QIDP asks the individual, guardian and prior providers how the person communicates and what language they use. The QIDP records the preferred communication mode, language, and any hearing, vision, speech or literacy needs in the entry record (REC-03).
The QIDP shares the communication profile with all staff and updates it when the person's needs change. The team records communication supports in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy.

The agency provides qualified interpreters (spoken and sign language) and translated documents whenever an individual or guardian needs them, at no cost. Staff do not use other residents, and do not rely on family members unless the person asks for it and the agency has offered a qualified interpreter.

Staff use the person's preferred mode for all important communications: rights, consents, Personal Plan meetings, medical information, complaints, restrictions and discharge. They give documents in large print, braille, plain language, pictures, audio or electronic format when needed, and check understanding.

The agency keeps communication devices, charged and in working order, within the individual's reach at all times. Staff do not remove or restrict access to a device except as an approved modification under RTS-02.
Staff learn each individual's communication method in orientation or through a staff-individual training before they work independently with that person (TRN-03).

The Administrator arranges access to interpreter and translation services, such as contracted providers or a language line, and keeps the contact details at each site. Staff are shown how to request them, including at night and on weekends.

Each year, the Administrator reviews each site against ADA accessibility standards for communal areas (entrances, bathrooms, hallways, kitchens, living areas). Barriers are recorded and removed on a written schedule. A person's access needs are met through reasonable accommodations.

The QIDP and Administrator consider any request for a reasonable accommodation from an individual or guardian within five working days and record the decision and the reason. If the request is denied, the person is told how to appeal under GPR-06.

Staff treat every individual with dignity and use respectful language. They do not use slurs, mocking or stereotyped statements, and they do not treat a person differently based on race, color, national origin, language, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, age, disability or diagnosis.

Staff report any suspected discrimination or denial of communication access to the Administrator the same day. The Administrator investigates, corrects the problem and records the outcome. Allegations of abuse, neglect or exploitation are reported under GPR-05.
The agency never retaliates against an individual, guardian or staff member who raises a discrimination concern.
All staff are trained on nondiscrimination, disability etiquette and communication supports at orientation and every year (TRN-04).
The Administrator reports communication access needs met, accommodation requests and discrimination complaints to the Quality Assurance committee at least quarterly (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures nondiscrimination practices, interpreter access, ADA accessibility and corrective action.
Records each individual's preferred communication mode and language, arranges supports, and decides accommodation requests with the Administrator.
Communicate with each individual in the preferred mode, keep devices available, and report discrimination or access barriers.
Receives reports on nondiscrimination and accessibility and supports the resources needed.

Entry record entry of preferred communication mode, language and sensory needs
Communication supports in the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
Interpreter and translation service requests and invoices
Accommodation request log with decisions and reasons
Annual ADA accessibility review for communal areas and barrier-removal schedule
Discrimination concern reports and corrective actions
Staff training records

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All employees, direct support professionals, nurses, QIDPs, contractors, volunteers, students and governing body members of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy, dignity and confidentiality of every individual served by [AGENCY NAME] in its Community Integrated Living Arrangement (CILA) homes. This covers each individual's personal space, communications, records and health information. The policy applies both the Illinois Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act and HIPAA.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] protects each individual's privacy and the confidentiality of all information about the individual. The Illinois Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Confidentiality Act (740 ILCS 110, incorporated by 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 115) and HIPAA (45 CFR Parts 160 and 164) both apply. When the two differ, the agency applies whichever gives the individual greater protection. CILA settings must protect privacy, dignity and respect (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200), and individuals have the rights described in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250. Each individual has privacy in sleeping and bathing areas and controls his or her own mail and telephone. Any restriction is handled only through the due process described in RTS-02. Authorized electronic monitoring is used only as 210 ILCS 165 allows and as described in GPR-10. Each individual or guardian receives a Notice of Privacy Practices. Suspected breaches are investigated and reported as HIPAA requires. Informed consent for any release of information is obtained before disclosure, except where law permits or requires disclosure without it.

definitions.definition: Any record or communication about an individual's services, health, behavior, finances, identity or personal life, in any form (paper, electronic, verbal).
Individually identifiable health information held or transmitted by the agency, as defined in 45 CFR Part 160.
An impermissible use or disclosure of PHI that compromises its security or privacy, as defined in 45 CFR Part 164, unless a low probability of compromise is shown by documented risk assessment.
Placement of an electronic monitoring device in an individual's room as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120 and 210 ILCS 165.
Consent given voluntarily by the individual or guardian after the information, risks and alternatives are explained in understandable terms. It includes consent for releases of information.
The person [AGENCY NAME] designates to receive privacy complaints, oversee breach response and maintain this policy.

procedures: The Governing Body designates [PRIVACY OFFICER NAME] as Privacy Officer and records the designation in the minutes. The Privacy Officer's name and [PHONE] appear in the Notice of Privacy Practices.

At entry, the QIDP or Administrator gives each individual and guardian the Notice of Privacy Practices, explains it in plain language or in the individual's preferred communication mode, and documents the date given and the acknowledgment in the record.

The QIDP obtains a written, signed and dated consent before releasing any record or information to anyone outside the Provider Support Team. Each consent names the recipient, the information, the purpose and the expiration. Releases not covered by a consent are made only when law permits or requires, and the reason is documented.

Before staff work alone, the Administrator trains each staff member, contractor and volunteer on this policy and requires a signed confidentiality statement for the personnel file. Training is repeated annually (see TRN-04).

Staff discuss an individual's health, behavior, finances or personal history only with those who need the information to provide supports. Staff do not discuss individuals in public places, in front of other individuals or visitors, or on social media.

Staff knock and wait for permission before entering an individual's bedroom or bathroom unless an emergency or a documented health and safety need requires immediate entry. Staff provide personal care in private with doors and curtains closed.

Each individual keeps control of his or her mail and telephone, including opening mail personally and making and receiving calls in private. Staff help only when the individual asks. Any limit on mail, phone or visitors is considered a rights restriction and follows RTS-02.

Records are kept as REC-01 requires. Paper records are in locked storage. Electronic records require individual log-ins and are never shared by password. Staff do not remove records from the home or office except as the Administrator authorizes in writing.

Staff do not photograph or record an individual, and do not use an individual's name or image in publicity or fundraising, without written consent from the individual or guardian that specifically permits it.

Before any electronic monitoring is considered, the QIDP follows GPR-10 and 210 ILCS 165. No device is placed in an individual's room without the consent and notice the Act requires. The consent is documented, and the individual may withdraw it as the Act allows. Roommates are given the notice and consent steps the Act requires.

On request, the individual or guardian may inspect and receive copies of the record as the Confidentiality Act and HIPAA allow. The QIDP logs each request and the response in the record. Any denial of access is reviewed by the Privacy Officer and explained in writing.

Any staff member who suspects a breach (lost record, misdirected fax or email, unauthorized access, lost device) reports it to the Privacy Officer immediately and no later than the end of the work shift.
The Privacy Officer opens a breach file within one business day, contains the problem, and completes a written risk assessment using the HIPAA factors.

If a breach of unsecured PHI is confirmed, the Privacy Officer notifies each affected individual (and guardian) in writing without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery. For breaches affecting 500 or more people, the Privacy Officer also notifies HHS and the media as 45 CFR Part 164 requires. For smaller breaches, the Privacy Officer logs them and reports them to HHS within 60 days after the end of the calendar year.

The Privacy Officer applies corrective action to the staff involved, up to and including termination. The Privacy Officer also records system fixes and reports each breach and its resolution to the Governing Body and the Quality Assurance process (QA-01).

No person is retaliated against for reporting a privacy concern. Individuals may raise privacy complaints under GPR-06 or to the Privacy Officer, and may contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of Inspector General or the Department. The Rights of Individuals form lists their addresses and phone numbers.

The Privacy Officer reviews this policy and the privacy practices in each home at least annually, and the Governing Body reviews the results. Documentation required by HIPAA is retained for at least six years.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy, designates the Privacy Officer, and reviews breach and compliance reports at least annually.
Ensures staff training, locked storage and secure systems, and enforces this policy through discipline.
Receives privacy complaints, investigates and reports breaches, maintains the breach log and the Notice of Privacy Practices.
Obtains consents, gives the Notice of Privacy Practices, handles record-access requests and monitors privacy in each home.
Protect privacy in daily supports, keep information confidential, and report suspected breaches the same shift.
