Signed releases of information
Staff confidentiality statements and training records
Record-access request log
Breach risk assessments, notifications and breach log
Privacy Officer designation
Electronic monitoring consent and notice documents, if any
Rights-restriction documentation under RTS-02, if any

policies.title: Person-Centered Planning, Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy
policies.applies_to: QIDPs, direct support professionals, nurses, the Administrator and every member of the Provider Support Team of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure every individual's supports are based on the person-centered Personal Plan developed with the Independent Service Coordination (ISC) agency, and that [AGENCY NAME] writes, delivers, shares and reviews the Implementation Strategy within the required timelines.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] follows the person-centered planning requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(1)-(3), 59 Ill. Adm. Code 120.160 and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230. The ISC leads Discovery and develops the Personal Plan, and has 30 calendar days after the person begins waiver services to complete both. The agency returns the Provider Signature Page to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The agency develops the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the QIDP's dated signature on the Provider Signature Page. The Implementation Strategy is based on the Personal Plan and assessments, and the individual and guardian take part in developing it. The individual or guardian signs it. The ISC does not sign or approve it. The individual, guardian and ISC each receive a copy of the strategy and every update. The strategy becomes part of the record. The QIDP reviews the strategy at least monthly and documents the review. Services we bill must be identified in the Personal Plan. The person's choices and preferences drive the plan, not staff convenience. The setting meets the HCBS requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)-(5) as incorporated in 59 Ill. Adm. Code Part 115.

definitions.definition: The person-centered plan developed by the ISC with the individual, guardian and team after Discovery. It identifies outcomes, services and supports, including the services this agency agrees to provide.
The agency's written plan on Form IL462-4470 for how it will support the outcomes in the Personal Plan that it agreed to support.
The ISC's person-centered process of learning the individual's preferences, strengths, needs and goals in order to develop the Personal Plan.
Independent Service Coordination agency that coordinates the individual's Personal Plan and waiver services.
Qualified Intellectual Disability Professional responsible for the Implementation Strategy and its monthly review.
The page on which the provider accepts the services it will provide under the Personal Plan.

procedures: On referral and admission, the Administrator tells the ISC the date services begin and gives the ISC a named agency contact. The ISC has 30 calendar days after services begin to complete Discovery and develop the Personal Plan. The QIDP takes part in the meetings the ISC schedules.

The QIDP attends Discovery and Personal Plan meetings, shares the individual's observed preferences, and makes sure the individual and guardian are heard. The QIDP uses the individual's own communication method and supports in decision-making (see RTS-03 and RTS-04).

Where the person is in crisis (homelessness, abuse or neglect), the QIDP cooperates with the ISC's Crisis Transition Plan and Funding Request and provides the information requested within the time the ISC sets.

On receipt of the Personal Plan, the QIDP records the date received on the cover sheet. The QIDP reviews the outcomes and services assigned to this agency and compares them to what the agency can deliver.
If the plan assigns a service the agency cannot provide, or omits a service the agency will bill, the QIDP tells the ISC in writing before signing and requests the needed change.
The QIDP signs and dates the Provider Signature Page and returns it to the ISC within 10 calendar days of receiving the Personal Plan. The QIDP keeps a copy in the record.
The QIDP calendars the Implementation Strategy due date as 20 calendar days after the QIDP's dated signature on the Provider Signature Page, and notes it on the QIDP tracking log.

With the Provider Support Team, the QIDP completes the Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470. It is based on the Personal Plan and assessments, and meets with the individual and guardian to develop it. The ISC is invited to take part as needed.
The strategy addresses every outcome the agency agreed to support. It states who provides each support, how often, how progress is measured, and what data is recorded.

For any individual who needs continuous supervision, the team assesses whether the person may be alone in the home or in the community independently. Any such time is based on assessed need and the person's preference, never staff convenience. The strategy states the time periods and locations involved, and the team documents its reasoning.

The QIDP reviews the strategy with the individual and guardian in language and format they understand. The individual or guardian signs and dates it. The QIDP does not obtain ISC signature or approval.

Within the same 20-day period, the QIDP gives a copy of the signed strategy to the individual, the guardian and the ISC, and documents the date and method of delivery. The strategy is filed in the record under REC-03.
Before staff provide supports, the QIDP trains each assigned DSP on the strategy and records the training (see TRN-03). Staff work from the current version.

At least once every month, the QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy against the daily documentation and progress data. The QIDP records whether outcomes are met, whether the supports still fit, and any change needed, then signs and dates the review.

When a revision is needed because of a change in condition, preference, outcome or service, the QIDP updates the strategy with the individual and guardian, obtains signatures, and gives the update to the individual, guardian and ISC. If the Personal Plan itself needs to change, the QIDP notifies the ISC.
The QIDP reports missed deadlines to the Administrator immediately. The Administrator takes corrective action and documents it. Timeliness is reported in the quality assurance review (QA-01).
At the annual Personal Plan meeting, the QIDP provides a summary of progress, outcomes and any recommended changes to the ISC and the team.

responsibilities.duty: Signs the Provider Signature Page, writes the Implementation Strategy, obtains signatures, distributes copies, trains staff, and reviews the strategy at least monthly.
Contributes assessments and recommendations, and carries out the strategy.
Ensures deadlines are met, resolves service gaps, and ensures billed services match the Personal Plan.
Take part in planning and sign the strategy. The agency supports them in doing so.
Completes Discovery and the Personal Plan and coordinates services. The ISC does not sign or approve the Implementation Strategy.

documentation: Personal Plan with date received
Provider Signature Page with QIDP's dated signature
Implementation Strategy on Form IL462-4470, signed by individual and guardian
Record of delivery of copies to individual, guardian and ISC
Monthly QIDP review notes, signed and dated
Strategy revisions and distribution records
Staff training on the strategy
QIDP deadline tracking log
Team assessment for time alone or independent community access, if applicable

policies.title: Provider Support Team, Assessments and Requests for Additional Supports
policies.applies_to: QIDPs, nurses, direct support professionals, other Provider Support Team members and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To establish a Provider Support Team for each individual, to base supports on current assessments, and to request additional staff resources or supports from the Department when an individual's needs exceed those in place.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a Provider Support Team for each individual, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220 requires. The team includes a QIDP and a direct support professional, plus a nurse or other professionals as the individual's needs require. The team is available 24 hours a day. The team is responsible for the service functions in the Personal Plan areas the agency covers and for developing the Implementation Strategy (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230). Assessments inform both the Personal Plan and the Implementation Strategy. When the individual needs more staff resources or supports than the current arrangement provides, the team requests additional supports from the Department under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.214. The Department responds as soon as possible and no later than ten business days after it receives the request. The need for non-base support hours is professionally reviewed at least annually and reported to the Department.

definitions.definition: The agency team for an individual, including at least a QIDP and a DSP, and a nurse or other professionals as needed. It develops and carries out the Implementation Strategy.
Staff hours or supports above those covered by the individual's base arrangement, requested because of assessed need.
A professional evaluation of an individual's health, functional, behavioral, communication, safety or other support needs, used to plan supports.
A written request by the team to the Department for extra staff resources or supports for an individual.

procedures: At admission, the Administrator names a Provider Support Team for each individual, including a QIDP, at least one DSP and, as needed, a nurse. Team names and roles are recorded in the individual's record and updated when members change.
The Administrator assigns a team contact to be reachable 24 hours a day. The agency posts the on-call number in each home and gives it to the individual and guardian. On-call responses are logged.
The team obtains and reviews the Personal Plan and assessments from the ISC and prior providers before developing the strategy (see PCS-01).

Within the time the team sets, the QIDP and nurse complete the assessments the individual needs. These may include health status, medication and side-effect monitoring, choking and seizure risk, behavior, communication, mobility, activities of daily living, safety and capacity to be alone. The agency also arranges other professional evaluations when they are indicated.

The nurse completes a health-risk review of each new individual and documents findings and recommendations for the team. The team uses these results to set health monitoring in the strategy (see HLT-02 and HLT-03).

The team provides care and supervision based on assessed needs. It helps individuals take part in community supports, advocates for them, helps them keep their comforts and safety, and provides counseling and crisis problem-solving.

The team helps individuals with activities of daily living and with assistive devices, and helps individuals get information about their medications, including observing and reporting effects and side effects (see HLT-01).
The team meets at least [FREQUENCY, e.g., monthly] and when needed, with the individual and guardian invited. Minutes record decisions, assignments and follow-up dates.

If assessment, incident data or staff observation shows the individual's needs exceed available staff resources or supports, the QIDP documents the need, including the assessment findings, the supports now in place, what is missing and the individual's request or preference.

The Administrator reviews and approves the request, and the QIDP submits it to the Department in the manner the Department directs. The QIDP notifies the individual, guardian and ISC and keeps a copy and the date of submission in the record. For intermittent-support rate determinations, the QIDP works with the ISC on the rate determination packet the ISC submits with the agency.
The QIDP calendars the Department's ten-business-day response date. If no response is received by that date, the QIDP contacts the Department and documents the follow-up.
While the request is pending, the team puts interim supports in place to protect health and safety, such as schedule changes, overtime or additional staff, and documents them.

When the Department responds, the QIDP shares the decision with the individual, guardian and ISC, and updates the Implementation Strategy if supports change. If the request is denied, the QIDP tells the individual and guardian of their right to raise concerns under GPR-06.

At least annually, the team professionally reviews the individual's need for non-base support hours. A QIDP or nurse signs the review. The Administrator reports the results to the Department and records the date and method of reporting.
The team reviews assessments again after any significant change of condition, hospitalization, incident or behavior change, and at least annually before the Personal Plan meeting.
The Administrator summarizes additional-support requests and outcomes in the quality assurance review (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Names team members, provides 24-hour availability, approves additional-support requests and reports annual review results to the Department.
Leads the team, coordinates assessments, prepares additional-support requests and tracks Department responses.
Completes health assessments and health-risk review and advises the team on health needs.
Contributes daily observations to the team and carries out supports.
Provide assessments and recommendations in their areas as requested.

documentation: Provider Support Team roster by individual
On-call log
Assessments and health-risk review
Team meeting minutes
Additional-support requests with dates submitted and Department responses
Interim support documentation
Annual non-base support hours review and report to the Department

policies.title: Implementation of Supports and Daily Documentation
policies.applies_to: Direct support professionals, QIDPs, nurses and the Administrator of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To make sure staff carry out the Implementation Strategy as written, record daily activity and progress, and bill only for services that appear in the Personal Plan.
policies.policy: Staff of [AGENCY NAME] carry out the outcomes and supports in each individual's Implementation Strategy and record daily activity as the strategy specifies. The QIDP signs and dates monthly progress documentation toward the Personal Plan outcomes. The agency's supports include help with activities of daily living and assistive devices, crisis problem-solving and advocacy (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Services billed must match the services identified in the Personal Plan. If a service change is needed, the agency tells the ISC (IDHS Person Centered Planning Policy and Guidelines). Direct care staff must demonstrate competence in the areas of the agency's required training, including documentation, before they work independently (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320).

definitions.definition: The staff record each shift of supports provided, the individual's participation, response, and any incident or change of condition, in the format the strategy specifies.
A monthly written summary of progress toward the Personal Plan outcomes, signed and dated by the QIDP.
A service the agency submits for payment. It must appear in the individual's Personal Plan.
Equipment such as a wheelchair, hearing aid, communication device or adaptive utensil used to support an individual's independence.

procedures: Before a DSP works independently with an individual, the QIDP reviews the current Implementation Strategy with the DSP, confirms competence, and records the review (see TRN-03). The strategy and daily documentation forms are kept in each home at [LOCATION].
Each shift, the DSP checks the home communication log and the strategy to identify planned activities, supports, health needs and appointments for the individuals supported that shift.
The DSP provides each support as the strategy states, in the individual's preferred way, and offers choices. The DSP does not substitute his or her own routine or preferences.
The DSP helps with activities of daily living as the individual needs and requests it, protecting privacy and dignity, and encourages the individual to do as much as the individual can independently.
The DSP checks that assistive devices are clean, working and available, and reports damage or need for replacement to the QIDP the same day.

When an individual is in distress or crisis, the DSP uses calm problem-solving and the strategies in the individual's plan. The DSP follows GPR-03 and GPR-04 for any behavioral intervention and contacts the on-call team member when the plan's steps are not enough.
The DSP advocates for the individual with providers, family and community members when the individual asks or needs it, and tells the QIDP of unresolved issues.

At the end of each shift, and no later than the shift's end, the DSP completes daily documentation in ink or the approved electronic system: the support provided, the individual's participation and response, data the strategy requires, and any health, safety or rights concerns. Entries are factual, dated, timed and signed (see REC-02).
The DSP does not pre-chart, backdate or document supports that were not provided. Errors are corrected with a single line, initial and date, or by the electronic audit trail.
The DSP reports incidents, changes of condition and suspected abuse or neglect immediately as GPR-05, HLT-03 and CI-01 direct, in addition to documenting them.
The home supervisor reviews daily documentation at least weekly for completeness and consistency with the strategy, signs the review, and corrects gaps with staff at once.

The QIDP reviews daily documentation and data at least monthly, compares them with Personal Plan outcomes, writes a progress summary, and signs and dates it. The QIDP records whether outcomes are being met and any change recommended.

When progress is not occurring, supports are not working or the individual's wishes have changed, the QIDP convenes the team, revises the strategy under PCS-01, and tells the ISC if the Personal Plan needs to change.

Before the agency bills for any service, the Administrator or billing staff confirm that the service is identified in the current Personal Plan and that daily documentation supports it (see FIN-01). If the individual receives a service not in the plan, the QIDP tells the ISC and asks for the plan change before billing.
Documentation is filed in the cumulative record as REC-03 requires and is available for review by the Department and other authorized reviewers.
The Administrator samples documentation each quarter and reports findings to the quality assurance process (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Provides supports as the strategy states, respects choices and privacy, and completes accurate, timely, signed daily documentation.
Reviews documentation weekly and corrects gaps on the spot.
Trains staff on the strategy, completes and signs the monthly progress summary, and revises the strategy when needed.
Ensures billing matches the Personal Plan and documentation, and reviews documentation quality.
Reviews health-related documentation and advises on health supports.

documentation: Implementation Strategy kept in each home
Daily shift documentation and data sheets
Home supervisor weekly review log
QIDP monthly progress summaries, signed and dated
Staff competence records on the strategy
Notices to the ISC about service changes
Billing-to-plan verification records

policies.title: Community Integration and Employment Choice
policies.applies_to: QIDPs, direct support professionals, the Administrator and the Provider Support Team of [AGENCY NAME]
policies.purpose: To support each individual to live as an integrated member of the community, with full community access and informed choices about work, day services, activities and relationships.
policies.policy: CILA settings and services must support integration and full community access, control of personal resources, privacy, dignity and respect, and freedom from coercion and restraint (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.200). [AGENCY NAME] optimizes individual initiative and autonomy. The homes are physically accessible, and communal areas meet ADA standards. Community integration, as defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120, is supported daily. Consistent with 42 CFR 441.301(c)(4)(i)-(ii), the individual's setting and supports provide opportunities to seek employment and work in competitive integrated settings, to engage in community life, and to choose among options. The CILA rate excludes day programs, which are billed separately. Each individual's choices about work, day program, activities and community access are documented in the Personal Plan. The Provider Support Team describes in the Implementation Strategy the supports that help the individual take part in community supports. Staff do not limit community access for staff convenience.

definitions.definition: As defined in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.120: the individual's participation in community life alongside people without disabilities, to the fullest extent the individual chooses.
Work in the community for at least minimum wage, alongside people without disabilities, with supports as needed.
A separately billed day service. It is not included in the CILA rate.
Activities, services, associations and resources in the community that the individual chooses to use.

procedures: During Discovery and the Personal Plan meeting, the QIDP asks each individual in the way the person understands best where, with whom and how the person wants to spend time, including work, volunteering, school, day program, faith, friends, family, recreation and shopping. Preferences are written in the individual's own words where possible.

The QIDP confirms that the Personal Plan records the individual's choices about work, day program, activities and community access. If it does not, the QIDP asks the ISC to add them. Informed choice includes information about options, including competitive integrated employment.

The QIDP separates the services the CILA provides from the day program. The agency does not bill day program time within the CILA rate. Where the individual attends a day program, the QIDP coordinates schedules and transportation with the day provider and records the arrangement.

If the individual wants to explore work, the QIDP refers the person to the ISC and appropriate employment resources and supports the individual in following through. The agency adjusts schedules, transportation and supports so work or job exploration can occur.

The Implementation Strategy states the supports the agency will provide to help the individual use community supports: transportation, accompaniment, skill teaching, communication aids and scheduling help. It names who provides each one.

Each week, staff and the individual plan the individual's schedule in the community based on the individual's choices. The schedule is posted in an accessible form. Individuals may change the plan at any time.

Staffing schedules are built around the individual's activities. A lack of staff, vehicles or convenience is not a reason to deny a community activity. If the agency cannot support a chosen activity, the QIDP records the barrier, arranges interim supports and requests additional supports under PCS-02.

Individuals may come and go, have visitors and use the community on a schedule they choose, as the Personal Plan states. Any limit is a rights restriction handled under RTS-02 and recorded with the supporting assessment.

Staff support individuals to build relationships with family, friends and neighbors, to join community groups and to use public places, businesses and services with the same access as other residents.
Staff support individuals' control of personal resources and money for community activities under FIN-03, and give help only as the individual wants and the plan states.

The QIDP keeps a record of each individual's community activities, employment and relationships and reviews it monthly with the individual (see PCS-01). Little or no community participation triggers a team review to find and remove barriers.
The home supervisor checks the home and vehicles weekly for accessibility and reports problems to the Administrator, who corrects them. Environmental access issues are also tracked under GPR-08.
At least annually, the QIDP asks each individual about satisfaction with community access and employment options and reports results to the Administrator and quality assurance process (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Elicits and documents choices, coordinates with the ISC and day and employment providers, and monitors community participation monthly.
Offer choices, support community activities and record participation.
Schedules staff and transportation to support individual choices and keeps homes and vehicles accessible.
Identifies barriers to integration and employment and develops solutions.

documentation: Personal Plan with documented choices about work, day program, activities and community access
Implementation Strategy sections on community supports
Weekly activity schedules
Community participation records
Coordination notes with day and employment providers
Records of any rights restriction under RTS-02
Annual satisfaction survey results

policies.title: Transition, Discharge and Termination of Services
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, QIDPs, Provider Support Team and all staff of [AGENCY NAME] involved in an individual's move or the end of services
policies.purpose: To protect each individual's right to remain in the CILA and, when a move or end of services occurs, to ensure it is planned with the individual, safe, timely and respectful of the individual's choices and rights.
policies.policy: Under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250, individuals have the right to remain in the CILA unless they voluntarily withdraw or meet the termination criteria in the Department's CILA rules. [AGENCY NAME] does not end services for staff convenience. The individual, guardian, ISC and Provider Support Team are involved in any transition. The agency gives written notice and a transition plan consistent with the person-centered planning requirements (42 CFR 441.301(c)(1), 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230). The agency stays responsible for affected individuals until they transition to another setting (see QA-02). Funds and property are returned at discharge with a signed inventory. The individual is told of rights and of how to contact the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of Inspector General and the Department.

definitions.definition: Any move of an individual to another residence or provider, or the end of CILA services, whether planned or urgent.
The individual's or guardian's own decision to leave the CILA, made with information about options.
An agency-initiated end of services, allowed only when the individual meets the Department's termination criteria.
A written plan covering the move: destination, supports, dates, medications, records, belongings, funds and who is responsible for each step.
A written list of the individual's funds and personal property, signed at return.

procedures: A transition begins when an individual or guardian says the person wants to leave, when the team believes the individual's needs can no longer be met safely, or when the agency considers ending services. The QIDP records the date and reason and tells the Administrator the same day.

The Administrator confirms that any agency-initiated termination meets the termination criteria in the Department's CILA rules before any step is taken. The Administrator documents the criteria and evidence, and the Governing Body is told of the decision. The agency first tries to resolve the problem by changing supports, requesting additional supports (PCS-02), or revising the strategy.

The QIDP notifies the individual, guardian and ISC promptly and meets with them. The meeting uses the individual's preferred communication method. The agency does not pressure individuals to leave and does not use the threat of discharge as coercion.

The Administrator gives written notice to the individual and guardian, with a copy to the ISC, stating the reason, the planned date and the individual's rights. The notice is given as early as possible and within the time frames the Department's rules require. It includes the address and telephone number of the Guardianship and Advocacy Commission, Equip for Equality, the Department's Office of Inspector General and the Department, as 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.250 requires.

The QIDP works with the ISC, who coordinates updates to the Personal Plan and identifies options. The team arranges visits to alternative settings so the individual can choose, and the individual's choice is recorded.

The QIDP prepares a written transition plan with the individual, guardian, ISC and Provider Support Team. The plan names the receiving provider or setting, the move date, who transports, who attends, and what supports are in place on day one.

The nurse prepares a health transfer summary: diagnoses, allergies, current medications and administration times, last dose, treatments, equipment, physician and appointment information, diet and risk plans. The nurse reviews medications with the receiving provider and sends the supply as law and policy allow (see HLT-01).

The QIDP sends the Implementation Strategy, behavior supports, communication information and other relevant records to the receiving provider only with a signed release or as the law permits (see RTS-05 and REC-04).

Before the move, staff help the individual pack and move all belongings. The Administrator and the individual or guardian complete an inventory of personal property and a reconciliation of personal funds (see FIN-03). Both sign it, and the receiving party or individual signs for return of funds and property. Any difference is documented and resolved before the funds are returned.

Staff keep supporting the individual with the same quality and staffing until the day of the move. The agency remains responsible for the individual until the person has transitioned to another setting, even if there is a dispute or a license or certification action is pending (see QA-02).

On the day of the move, a staff member accompanies the individual if the individual wishes and hands off verbally to the receiving staff. The QIDP records the time, the people present and what was transferred.
The QIDP follows up with the individual and the receiving provider within [NUMBER, e.g., 7] days after the move to ask how the person is doing and offer information. The follow-up is recorded.

If the individual moves in an emergency (hospitalization, safety risk), the QIDP follows these steps as soon as is practical, notifies the guardian and ISC at once, and documents why the normal timeline could not be followed.

The QIDP completes a discharge summary within [NUMBER, e.g., 30] days covering the reason, services provided, progress and the destination. The Administrator notifies the Department and others as required (see REC-04) and closes the record for retention under REC-04.
If an individual dies, CI-04 applies instead of this policy.
The Administrator reports all transitions and any agency-initiated terminations to the Governing Body and quality assurance process (QA-01) and checks that each followed this policy.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies termination criteria, issues written notices, arranges the return of funds and property and informs the Governing Body.
Coordinates the transition plan with the individual, guardian and ISC, sends records, and completes follow-up and the discharge summary.
Prepares the health transfer summary and medication handoff.
Supports the individual and keeps services in place until the move occurs.
Coordinates the Personal Plan changes and the search for another setting.

documentation: Record of reason for transition and date
Documentation of termination criteria review (agency-initiated)
Written notice with rights and contact information
Transition plan
Health transfer summary and medication handoff record
Signed releases for records sent
Signed inventory of funds and property
Follow-up record
Discharge summary
Report to the Governing Body

policies.title: Medication Administration, Medical Services and Staff Certification
policies.applies_to: All CILA sites; all direct support professionals, QIDPs, nurses, Program Directors, contractors and volunteers who give, supervise or assist with medications or arrange medical services
policies.purpose: To make sure medical services and medications for each individual are directed by a licensed physician, given only by staff who are properly certified, and monitored for safety, effects and side effects, as required of a licensed CILA provider in Illinois.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] certifies that any medical service or medication it provides, or whose administration it supervises, is carried out under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116 (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240). A licensed physician (MD or DO) is responsible for each individual's medical services, including prescribing. A physician examines an individual before any psychotropic medication is started. AIMS screening is completed at least every six months for each individual who takes psychotropic medication. A physician reviews each individual's medications and sees the individual at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires. Only direct care staff who have completed the Nurse-Trainer program under Part 116 may administer medications or supervise self-administration (see TRN-05). The Provider Support Team helps each individual get medication information, and staff observe and report medication effects and side effects (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). The agency's RN completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars (IDHS New Provider Guidance for CILA). Medications are never used as punishment, for staff convenience or as a substitute for supports. Any medication used to control behavior is also governed by GPR-03, GPR-04, RTS-02 and RTS-03.

definitions.definition: A medication prescribed to affect mood, thought, behavior or mental state, including antipsychotic, antidepressant, anti-anxiety, mood-stabilizing and similar medications.
Abnormal Involuntary Movement Scale, a standardized screening for movement disorders such as tardive dyskinesia, used for individuals taking psychotropic medication.
Direct care staff who have been trained and certified by the agency's RN under 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116 to administer medications or supervise self-administration.
Medication Administration Record, the written record kept for each individual that shows each medication given, the date and time, and the staff who gave it.
The team maintained for each individual that includes a QIDP, a DSP, and a nurse or other professionals as needed.

procedures: At entry, the QIDP collects the individual's current medication list, prescriber orders, allergies, pharmacy, and the name and contact information of the physician (MD/DO) responsible for medical services. The QIDP files these in the record the same day (see REC-03).

The agency's RN confirms with the guardian and individual who the responsible physician is, and the Program Director records this on the individual's health face sheet. If the individual has no physician, the PST arranges one before or immediately after admission and documents the arrangement.

The RN schedules and tracks each individual's required physician visit and medication review at least every six months, or more often if a psychiatrist requires. The RN keeps a health calendar and gives the Program Director a monthly list of upcoming and overdue visits.
Staff give or help with medications only on a current written prescriber order and from the pharmacy-labeled container. Staff never change a dose, time or route on their own.

The Program Director keeps a current roster of Nurse-Trainer certified staff, with certification dates, and checks it before each schedule is finalized. A staff person who is not certified does not administer medications or supervise self-administration (see TRN-05).

Before a psychotropic medication is started, the RN confirms that a physician examination has been completed and documented. The RN also confirms that informed consent has been obtained from the individual and guardian as required (RTS-03). If the medication is used to address behavior, the RN refers the matter to the Behavior Management Committee (GPR-03) and applies RTS-02.

The RN schedules AIMS screening at least every six months for each individual on psychotropic medication. A trained clinician completes it, the physician receives the results, and the RN files the completed form in the record. If a screening is missed, the RN reschedules it within seven days and notifies the Administrator.

For individuals who self-administer, the PST assesses the individual's ability and the supports needed, and the RN documents the assessment. Only Nurse-Trainer certified staff supervise self-administration, and the Implementation Strategy states the level of support.

Staff record each medication on the MAR immediately after it is given, with the date, time and their initials. Staff never pre-chart or chart later from memory. Any missed dose is explained on the MAR.

Staff observe each individual for effects and side effects of medication and record observations in the daily notes. Staff report concerns to the RN by the end of the shift, or immediately if the concern is serious, so the RN can contact the physician.

Staff and the RN help each individual and guardian get medication information, including the purpose, expected effects, side effects and alternatives, in a form the individual can understand (RTS-04). The RN records this teaching.

PRN medications are given only on a written physician protocol that states the reason, dose and limits, and the staff person documents the reason and the result each time. Psychotropic PRN use must be reviewed by the RN within one business day.
If an individual refuses a medication, staff do not force or hide it. Staff document the refusal, notify the RN, and the RN advises the physician and guardian as needed.

Staff keep medications locked and separate for each individual. The RN or Program Director checks storage and the counts of controlled medications at each shift change and records them on the count sheet.
When an individual leaves the site for a visit, work or community activity, the medications and instructions go with the individual only through a documented process approved by the RN.

Medication errors are reported to the RN right away. The RN or staff contact the physician or poison control as needed (see HLT-03), and staff complete a critical incident report under CI-01. The RN reports any reportable event under CI-02. The RN analyzes errors monthly for trends.
Each month, the RN reviews MARs and the QIDP reviews the Implementation Strategy for medication-related outcomes. The RN presents medication error, AIMS and visit-compliance data to QA (QA-01).
The RN safely disposes of discontinued or expired medication as the pharmacy and agency written procedures direct, with two staff witnessing and documenting the disposal.

responsibilities.duty: Certifies compliance with the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and Part 116; makes sure an RN and enough certified staff are available.
Trains and certifies staff, oversees medication practice, tracks physician visits and AIMS screenings, reviews MARs and errors.
Is responsible for medical services and prescribing; examines before psychotropics begin; reviews medications and sees the individual at least every six months.
Obtains orders and consents at entry, includes medication supports in the Implementation Strategy, reviews it monthly.
Maintains the roster of certified staff, schedules only certified staff to give medications, checks MARs and storage.
Give or supervise medications only if Nurse-Trainer certified; document accurately; observe and report effects and side effects.

documentation: Physician orders and responsible-physician designation in the record
Medication Administration Records
Controlled medication count sheets
Nurse-Trainer certification roster and training records
Completed AIMS forms with dates
Physician visit and medication review notes
Informed consent for psychotropic medication
Medication error and critical incident reports
Monthly RN review notes and QA data

policies.title: Nursing Oversight and Health Care Coordination
policies.applies_to: Agency RN and nursing contractors, Provider Support Teams, QIDPs, Program Directors and direct support professionals at all CILA sites
policies.purpose: To provide qualified nursing oversight of each individual's health and medications and to coordinate physician, dental and specialist care with the Provider Support Team so health needs are met in a timely way.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] employs or contracts with a registered nurse who holds a current, unencumbered Illinois license and who has completed the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars (IDHS New Provider Guidance for CILA). The RN trains and evaluates direct care staff on medications and reviews health records. A nurse serves on the Provider Support Team as needed for each individual (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). The RN coordinates physician, dental and specialist care with the Provider Support Team. Staff help individuals get medication information and observe and report medication effects and side effects (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Medical services and medications are provided under the Mental Health and Developmental Disabilities Administrative Act and 59 Ill. Adm. Code 116, as certified in 59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.240.

definitions.definition: An Illinois nursing license that has no discipline, probation, suspension, or conditions limiting practice.
The DHS/Division of Developmental Disabilities webinars that an agency RN must complete to be approved to train direct care staff to administer medications.
Scheduling, communicating about and following up on medical, dental, vision, behavioral health and specialist services so recommendations are carried out and recorded.

procedures: Before the first admission, the Administrator hires or contracts with an RN, verifies the Illinois license online with the state licensing authority, and files a copy of the verification in the personnel record (STF-01, STF-05).
The RN completes the DHS/DDD RN trainer webinars and keeps proof of completion in the personnel file. The Administrator confirms completion before the RN trains any staff.

The Administrator re-verifies the RN's license status at least annually and any time the agency learns of a complaint or discipline. If a license becomes encumbered, the RN stops training staff immediately and the Administrator arranges a replacement RN within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days and reports as required.

The RN completes a health assessment for each individual within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days of admission, using the physician's information, history and the PST's assessments. The RN records the assessment in the record and shares relevant findings with the QIDP for the Implementation Strategy.

The RN joins the Provider Support Team for each individual as needed, and attends meetings when health issues, medication changes or health-related requests for additional supports are discussed (PCS-02).
The RN trains and evaluates direct care staff on medication administration under TRN-05 and Part 116, observes practice at each site, and documents each observation and any corrective follow-up.

The RN reviews each individual's health record at least monthly, including MARs, daily notes, incident reports, vital signs and weights, appointment outcomes and follow-up of physician orders. The RN documents the review in the record.

The RN and the QIDP maintain a health calendar for each individual covering annual physical exams, physician medication reviews at least every six months, AIMS screening, dental, vision, hearing, immunizations and age-appropriate screenings. The Program Director arranges appointments and transportation.

Before each appointment, the staff person who is going or arranging transportation completes the appointment form noting concerns, changes and questions. After the appointment, staff return with written orders and instructions and give them to the RN the same day.
The RN reviews new orders within one business day, transcribes them to the MAR or care plan as required, notifies the guardian, informs staff and arranges any training needed.
Staff observe and report medication effects and side effects as described in HLT-01. The RN reviews reports each week, contacts the physician when needed, and records the contact.
The RN helps each individual and guardian get medication information and teaches in a form the individual understands, using communication supports identified in the Personal Plan (RTS-04).

For specialist care, including psychiatry, neurology, dentistry, therapy and others, the RN or QIDP sends needed records, confirms attendance, and obtains written recommendations. The RN tracks recommendations to completion or documents why they were not carried out.

When an individual is hospitalized or goes to an emergency room, the RN or on-call nurse contacts the hospital within [NUMBER OF HOURS] hours, sends the medication list and health information, takes part in discharge planning, and updates the PST and Implementation Strategy on return (HLT-03, PCS-05).
The RN provides health-related training on individual-specific needs, such as seizures, dysphagia, diabetes and other conditions, and documents who was trained and when (TRN-03).
The RN provides a monthly health summary to the Administrator and QA committee, covering missed appointments, medication errors, hospitalizations, infections and health trends (QA-01).
The RN provides 24-hour on-call guidance to staff, and the on-call schedule is posted at each site with phone numbers ([PHONE]).

responsibilities.duty: Hires and verifies the RN's license and webinar completion; makes sure nursing time is enough for the number of individuals served.
Trains and evaluates staff, reviews health records, coordinates health care, advises the PST and physicians, and provides on-call guidance.
Includes health supports in the Implementation Strategy, coordinates with the RN and guardians.
Schedules appointments and transportation, makes sure orders are carried out.
Accompany individuals to appointments as assigned, report changes, effects and side effects, follow health care instructions.

documentation: RN license verification and DHS/DDD RN trainer webinar completion
RN health assessments
Monthly record reviews
Staff observation and evaluation forms
Health calendars
Appointment forms and physician orders
Hospital and emergency contact notes
Monthly nursing summary to QA

policies.title: Health Monitoring, Seizures, Choking Risk, Change of Condition and Emergency Medical Care
policies.applies_to: All direct support professionals, QIDPs, Program Directors, nurses and on-call staff at all CILA sites
policies.purpose: To make sure staff recognize and respond to changes in health, medical and psychiatric emergencies, seizures and choking risks, and that guardians, the RN and the physician are told promptly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] monitors each individual's health in line with the Personal Plan and Implementation Strategy and the care and supervision that the Provider Support Team provides based on assessed needs (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Staff and individuals know how to react to psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Each site has an operational telephone that is accessible to staff and individuals, with the site's phone number and the nearest poison control center posted (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). The agency obtains consent to emergency medical services at entry, and files it in the record with other required entry documents (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115). Each individual's seizure risk and choking risk plans are written in the record, and staff are trained on them before working with the individual. When an individual's condition changes, staff notify the guardian, RN and physician. Staff report any critical incident under CI-02. If a guardian or parent is notified of an allegation of abuse or neglect, the notification occurs within 24 hours of the agency receiving it (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320), as described in GPR-05.

definitions.definition: Any new or worsening sign, symptom, behavior, function or mood that differs from the individual's usual baseline, including injury, illness, fever, changes in appetite, sleep, mobility, alertness, seizure pattern, breathing or swallowing.
A written individualized plan, signed or approved by the physician and RN, that describes the individual's seizure types, triggers, first aid, rescue medication, when to call 911 and how to document.

A written individualized plan, based on physician, dietitian or therapist recommendations, that states diet texture, positioning, supervision, pacing and emergency response for choking or aspiration risk.

A condition that may threaten life, limb or function and needs immediate medical care, including unresponsiveness, breathing problems, choking, severe bleeding, seizure that does not stop, stroke signs, chest pain, poisoning or serious injury.

procedures: At entry, the QIDP obtains consent to emergency medical services signed by the individual or guardian as appropriate, along with emergency contacts, physician, insurance and allergy information. The QIDP files them in the record and puts a current emergency face sheet at the site for use in an emergency (REC-03).

The Program Director checks that each site has an operational telephone accessible to staff and individuals, and that the site address, site phone number and nearest poison control center are posted. The Program Director checks this at least monthly and records the check.

Before an individual's first unsupervised shift with staff, the RN and QIDP identify seizure and choking risks from the physician's information, assessments and history. When a risk is identified, the RN writes the plan with the physician's input and files it in the record.

The RN trains each direct care staff person on each seizure and choking plan before the staff person works alone with the individual, and again on any change. The RN documents the training with staff signatures and dates (TRN-02, TRN-03).

Staff are trained on how to react to psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths. They also learn CPR, first aid and choking response under TRN-02, and review these emergency procedures at site meetings at least annually.

In a medical emergency, staff call 911 first, begin first aid or CPR, and stay with the individual. They then call the on-call nurse or RN ([PHONE]) and the Program Director. Staff send the emergency face sheet, medication list and consent with the individual to the hospital, and a staff person accompanies the individual unless emergency responders advise otherwise.

In a psychiatric emergency, staff use the individual's behavior support plan and crisis problem-solving strategies, keep the individual and others safe, and call 911 if there is imminent danger. Staff also notify the on-call nurse and Program Director. Restraint or seclusion may be used only as permitted in GPR-04.

In a suspected poisoning or medication overdose, staff call the poison control center at the posted number, follow its instructions, and call 911 if directed or if the individual is symptomatic. They notify the RN and complete an incident report.

During a seizure, staff follow the individual's seizure plan, time the seizure, protect the individual from injury, and document it on the seizure record, including date, time, duration, type, rescue medication given, recovery and any injury. Staff call 911 when the plan directs or when the seizure lasts longer than the plan states, or when injury or breathing trouble occurs.

For choking risk, staff apply the individual's plan at every meal and snack, including diet texture, position, rate, supervision and adaptive equipment. If choking occurs, staff apply the choking response they were trained in and call 911 even if the obstruction is cleared and the individual appears well.

Staff observe each individual daily for changes in condition and record what they see in the daily notes. Staff measure and record weight, vital signs and other items the physician or RN orders, on the schedule ordered.

When a change of condition is noted, staff tell the on-call nurse or RN right away. The nurse gives instructions, and the RN or designee tells the physician as appropriate. Staff notify the guardian as soon as practical and no later than [NUMBER OF HOURS] hours after the change, and document the notification in the record.

If an injury is of unknown origin, or there are signs of possible abuse, neglect or exploitation, staff also follow GPR-05. The agency tells the guardian or parent of the allegation within 24 hours of receiving it (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.320).

Staff report any critical incident, including serious injury, hospitalization, medication error with harm or an emergency room visit, to the Program Director immediately, and the Program Director reports it under CI-01 and CI-02, including to law enforcement, DHS OIG and CIRAS as those policies direct.
If an individual dies, staff call 911, begin emergency care unless there are valid orders otherwise, notify the Administrator, and follow CI-04.

After any emergency or change of condition, the RN reviews the event within one business day, updates the health plan, seizure plan or choking plan if needed, and informs the Provider Support Team and QIDP so the Implementation Strategy can be revised (PCS-01, PCS-03).
The RN and Administrator review incidents, ER visits and hospitalizations each month for trends and present them to the QA committee (QA-01).

responsibilities.duty: Observe, respond to and report health changes and emergencies; follow seizure and choking plans; document accurately.
Writes seizure and choking plans, trains staff, gives on-call advice, reviews events and informs the physician.
Obtains emergency medical consent at entry, updates Implementation Strategy, notifies guardians.
Maintains site phone and posted numbers, makes sure staff training is current, reports critical incidents.
Makes sure reporting occurs under CI-02 and that notifications to guardians and agencies are timely.

documentation: Consent to emergency medical services
Emergency face sheet
Seizure plans and seizure records
Choking risk plans and training sign-in sheets
Daily notes
Guardian, RN and physician notification entries
Critical incident reports
Monthly phone and poison control posting checks
RN event reviews and QA data

policies.title: Emergency Preparedness and Fire Drills
policies.applies_to: All CILA sites, all staff, individuals, volunteers and contractors; the Administrator, Program Directors and the RN
policies.purpose: To make sure each CILA site is ready for fire, severe weather, other disasters and public health crises, and that staff and individuals know how to evacuate or shelter safely.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a disaster preparedness plan that covers disasters and public health crises and reviews it at least annually (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Staff and individuals know how to react to fire, severe weather, missing persons, psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths. Staff are trained on the location of fire extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes. Evacuation drills include actual evacuation to safe areas. Corrective actions for drill or inspection deficiencies are recorded. Each site has at least one approved fire extinguisher with an annual inspection tag. Red Cross-standard first aid kits are checked quarterly and restocked. New individuals are trained within 30 days of moving in. Fire and disaster training records are available at the site to the Division of Developmental Disabilities and BALC. Residences comply with local building codes (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115). Life-safety code and siting requirements are in GPR-08.

definitions.definition: A practice of the site's fire or emergency evacuation plan in which staff and individuals actually leave the building to a designated safe area.

The agency's written plan for fire, severe weather, power or water loss, other disasters and public health crises such as epidemics, including sheltering, evacuation, communication and supply procedures.
A first aid kit with contents that meet the American Red Cross standard for a workplace or home kit.
A location outside the building or other designated place, identified in the plan, where all occupants gather for a head count.

procedures: Before the first admission at each site, the Administrator and Program Director write a site-specific emergency plan with an evacuation floor plan showing at least two exits from each level and sleeping area, the safe area, locations of extinguishers and first aid kits, and utility shut-offs. The plan is posted at the site.

The Administrator maintains one agency disaster preparedness plan covering fire, severe weather, power or water loss, other disasters and public health crises. The Administrator and RN review and update it at least annually and after any actual emergency, and record the date and the changes.

Each plan addresses each individual's needs for evacuation, including mobility, hearing, vision, communication, medication and behavior needs. The QIDP records these in the Implementation Strategy and the RN gives input where needed. Staff know what help each person needs.

The Program Director confirms that each site has an operational telephone and a posted list showing the site phone number and the nearest poison control center, as well as emergency numbers, the on-call nurse and the Administrator ([PHONE]).

The Program Director holds evacuation drills at the frequency required by the State Fire Marshal, local fire authority and BALC. Drills are held on all shifts and at varied times, including when individuals are asleep. Each drill includes actual evacuation of staff and individuals to the safe area, and uses more than one exit route over time.

For each drill, the staff person in charge records the date, time, shift, weather, staff and individuals present, time to evacuate, participation, problems seen and the staff person's signature. The Program Director reviews the form within three business days.

If a drill or an inspection finds a deficiency, the Program Director writes the corrective action, the person responsible and the date it was corrected, and keeps the record at the site. The Administrator confirms the correction within [NUMBER OF DAYS] days and repeats the drill if the problem affected evacuation.

The Program Director checks that each site has at least one approved fire extinguisher with a current annual inspection tag. The Program Director also checks it monthly for pressure, access and visible condition, and arranges service or replacement before the tag expires.

The Program Director or designee checks each first aid kit at least quarterly against a contents list, restocks and replaces expired items, and records the date and initials on the kit log. Staff restock used items right after any use.

Each new staff person is trained on the location of extinguishers, first aid kits and evacuation routes, and on how to respond to fire, severe weather, missing persons, psychiatric and medical emergencies, poison control and deaths during orientation and before working alone (TRN-01, TRN-02).

Each new individual is trained in how to respond to fire and disasters within 30 days of moving in, in a way suited to the person's communication and learning needs. The QIDP or Program Director records the training, and repeats it at least annually and as needed.

Staff respond to fire by getting everyone out, calling 911 from a safe place, closing doors when possible, accounting for each individual at the safe area, and notifying the Program Director and Administrator. In severe weather, staff move individuals to the designated shelter area and use the weather alert method named in the plan.
For a missing person, staff follow CI-03. For a medical or psychiatric emergency, staff follow HLT-03. For a death, staff follow CI-04.

Each site keeps copies of fire, building, local and State health, sanitation and environmental inspections, and records of corrective actions. The Program Director files new reports within five business days of receipt (GPR-08, ENV-02).
Fire and disaster training records, drill records and the disaster plan are kept at the site and are available to the Division of Developmental Disabilities and BALC on request.
The Administrator checks the site records at least quarterly. The Administrator reports drill completion, corrective actions, and training status to the QA committee (QA-01).

In a public health crisis, the Administrator and RN apply the disaster plan's provisions on infection control, staffing, supplies, communication with guardians and public health authorities, and ongoing community integration and rights protections (ENV-02, RTS-01).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains and annually reviews the disaster preparedness plan; verifies corrective actions; ensures compliance with code and inspection requirements.
Conducts and records drills, checks extinguishers and first aid kits, trains staff and individuals, keeps site records.
Advises on evacuation needs of individuals and on the public health crisis parts of the plan.
Records individual evacuation needs in the Implementation Strategy and helps train individuals.
Know and follow the plan, take part in drills, account for each individual in an emergency.

documentation: Site emergency plan with floor plan
Annual disaster preparedness plan review record
Evacuation drill records and corrective action records
Fire extinguisher inspection tags and monthly check log
Quarterly first aid kit check log
Staff and individual fire and disaster training records
Posted phone and poison control list check
Copies of inspection reports
QA reports on drills and corrective actions

policies.title: Infection Prevention and Control
policies.applies_to: All CILA sites, employees, contractors, volunteers, respite guests and individuals; the RN, Program Directors and the Administrator
policies.purpose: To prevent and control the spread of infection in CILA homes, to protect staff from bloodborne pathogens and to meet the respite health requirements in Illinois rules, while respecting the rights of individuals.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] follows standard precautions and hand hygiene practices in every home. The agency's disaster preparedness plan covers public health crises and is reviewed annually (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Copies of local and State health, sanitation and environmental inspections are kept at the site (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300). Before respite begins, the agency obtains a physician statement that the individual has no contagious disease, and documents that the individual will not jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home. Respite longer than two weeks requires Department approval before the initial two weeks end, and is allowed only in emergencies (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.205). The agency complies with the OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030, including an exposure control plan, training, and the protective equipment and vaccination offers that standard requires for employees with occupational exposure. Infection control measures are applied in the least restrictive way possible, and any limit on an individual's rights is handled under RTS-02.

definitions.definition: Basic infection control practices used with every individual, including hand hygiene, use of gloves and other protective equipment when exposure is possible, safe handling of sharps and waste, cleaning and disinfection, and respiratory etiquette.
Microorganisms in human blood, such as hepatitis B virus, hepatitis C virus and HIV, that can cause disease in people.

The written plan required by 29 CFR 1910.1030 that identifies employees with occupational exposure and describes how exposure is prevented, how it is handled when it occurs, and how it is followed up.
Short-term care and supports provided to an individual in a CILA home, to give relief to caregivers or for other planned or emergency needs (see GPR-07).

procedures: The Administrator and RN write the agency's infection control procedures and exposure control plan, and review them at least annually, and after any outbreak or exposure event. The review is recorded.

During orientation, and annually after that, the RN trains all direct care staff on standard precautions, hand hygiene, safe cleaning and disinfection, laundry, waste handling, food hygiene, and the exposure control plan. The RN uses sign-in sheets and records the training in each personnel file (TRN-01, TRN-02, STF-05).

The Administrator makes sure that employees with occupational exposure are offered hepatitis B vaccination at no cost, as 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires, and records acceptance or declination in the personnel record. Employees also receive post-exposure evaluation and follow-up when exposed.

Each site stocks gloves, masks, hand hygiene supplies, disinfectants, sharps containers where needed, and spill kits. The Program Director checks supplies weekly and restocks as needed, and records the check.

Staff wash or sanitize their hands before and after giving care, before preparing or serving food, after toileting assistance, after contact with body fluids and after removing gloves. Staff use gloves and other protective equipment when exposure to blood or body fluids is possible.

Staff clean and disinfect high-touch surfaces, bathrooms and the kitchen on the written cleaning schedule, using products approved for the purpose, and initial the cleaning log. They handle spills of blood or body fluids using the spill kit and dispose of waste as the exposure control plan states.

If a staff person has an exposure incident, the person washes the area at once, reports to the Program Director and RN the same shift, and gets medical evaluation as the plan states. The Program Director completes an exposure report within 24 hours and the RN follows up and keeps the report confidential.

Staff who have signs of a contagious illness, such as fever, vomiting, diarrhea or a rash that could spread, do not work in the home until they are well enough or cleared under the agency's written exclusion guidelines. Staff report illness to the Program Director before the shift.

When an individual shows signs of infection, staff notify the RN, who contacts the physician and guides care. The RN may recommend precautions, such as separate use of a bathroom or masks, that are used only as needed, for the shortest time and in the least restrictive way. Any restriction on movement or visitors is handled under RTS-02 and the individual and guardian are told.
The RN tracks infections and outbreaks, and notifies the local health department when reporting is required. The Administrator reports any event that is a critical incident under CI-01 and CI-02.

For respite, before the stay begins, the QIDP obtains a physician's statement that the individual has no contagious disease and files it in the respite record. The QIDP also documents that the individual will not jeopardize the health or safety of others in the home (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.205). If either is missing, the respite stay does not begin.

If a respite stay may last more than two weeks, the Administrator contacts the Department before the initial two weeks end to request approval. This is allowed only in emergencies. The Administrator documents the request, the response and the dates (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.205, GPR-07).

Each site keeps copies of local and State health, sanitation and environmental inspection reports. The Program Director files them within five business days of receipt and writes corrective actions for any deficiency (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.300, GPR-08).

In a public health crisis, the Administrator and RN activate the disaster preparedness plan, follow guidance from public health authorities, and tell guardians and individuals in plain language. They keep access to rights, community and visitors to the greatest extent allowed (ENV-01, RTS-01).
The RN offers and helps arrange immunizations recommended by the individual's physician and public health authorities, with consent of the individual or guardian. The RN records declinations.
The Administrator reviews infection data, exposure reports and cleaning log compliance each quarter and presents them to the QA committee (QA-01). TB screening for employees follows STF-05.

policies.title: Food, Nutrition and Modified Diets
policies.applies_to: All CILA sites; direct support professionals, QIDPs, Program Directors, the RN, and individuals and guardians
policies.purpose: To make sure individuals have nutritious food of their choice, with access to food at all times, and that modified diets and choking-risk precautions are ordered, written down, posted and followed safely.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] provides care and supervision based on assessed needs, helps individuals with activities of daily living and keeps their safety and comforts (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.220). Dietary needs, including any modified diet, are written in the Implementation Strategy, which the agency develops on Form IL462-4470 within 20 calendar days of the provider's dated signature on the Personal Plan, and the QIDP reviews at least monthly (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115.230). Modified diets are based on a physician's or dietitian's order. Individuals choose their own meals and snacks and have access to food, consistent with HCBS settings requirements (RTS-01). Choking-risk food textures and aspiration precautions are posted for staff in the home. Any restriction on food is a rights modification and must follow RTS-02. The individual's record and Implementation Strategy are kept in the manner required by Part 115 (59 Ill. Adm. Code 115).

definitions.definition: A diet ordered by a physician or dietitian that changes the type, texture, amount or content of food or liquids, such as pureed, mechanical soft, thickened liquids, diabetic, low sodium, allergen-free or calorie-controlled.
Steps to reduce the risk of food, liquid or saliva entering the airway, including upright positioning, slow pace, small bites, supervision and staying upright after meals.
Any limit on an individual's choice of or access to food, or the timing or amount of food, that is not an ordered medical diet requested or accepted by the individual or guardian.
A swallowing disorder that may require a speech-language pathologist evaluation and a modified diet.

procedures: At entry and at least annually, the RN and QIDP gather information on each individual's food preferences, culture and religion, allergies, intolerances, weight history, swallowing and chewing, need for assistance, medications that affect eating, and any physician or dietitian orders. The QIDP files the information in the record.

When there is a possible swallowing or choking risk, the RN asks the physician to order an evaluation by a speech-language pathologist or dietitian. The RN keeps the written recommendations and orders in the record.

When a modified diet is ordered by the physician or dietitian, the RN and QIDP put the diet, texture, liquid consistency, positioning, supervision level, adaptive equipment and emergency response into the Implementation Strategy and the choking risk plan (HLT-03). The QIDP updates the Implementation Strategy and gives the individual and guardian a copy.

The RN posts a one-page diet and texture sheet in the kitchen and dining area, with the individual's name and photo or other identifier as the individual agrees, showing diet, textures to avoid, thickened liquids, positioning and the steps staff take if choking occurs. The RN replaces the sheet within one business day of any order change.

The RN trains each staff person on each individual's diet and aspiration precautions before the staff person works alone, and again on any change. The RN records the training with staff signatures (TRN-03).

Each individual, with staff support as needed, chooses the foods, meals, mealtimes and place to eat. Staff help the individual plan menus, shop and cook as the individual wishes, in line with the Personal Plan. Menus are not set by staff alone or on a fixed schedule that limits choice.

Individuals have access to food and drink at any time, including snacks and meals outside of regular times, unless there is a documented restriction handled under RTS-02. Staff do not lock the kitchen or refrigerator, or take away food as a consequence, except under RTS-02.

Staff offer healthy choices and information about nutrition in a way the individual understands, and respect the individual's decisions, including a decision to eat foods that are not on a recommended diet, with informed consent supports under RTS-03. If a choice creates a health risk, staff tell the RN, who talks with the individual and guardian and the physician, and documents the discussion.

Staff follow the posted diet sheet at every meal and snack, give the right textures, stay with the individual as required, and document meals, intake and any problems as ordered in the daily notes (PCS-03).

Staff store, prepare and serve food safely. They wash hands, keep cold food at 40 degrees Fahrenheit or colder and hot food at 135 degrees Fahrenheit or hotter, label and date leftovers, and clean surfaces. The Program Director checks refrigerator temperatures and food storage weekly and records them.
Staff identify and keep allergens away from individuals with food allergies, read labels, and follow the allergy response plan. If an allergic reaction occurs, staff call 911 and follow HLT-03.

The RN weighs individuals on the schedule ordered by the physician, and at least monthly where there is a nutrition or swallowing concern. The RN reviews weights, intake and signs of dehydration, and tells the physician about unplanned weight loss or gain.

If staff think a food restriction is needed for safety, such as locking food for an individual with a medical condition like Prader-Willi syndrome, the QIDP and RN bring it to the Provider Support Team. The restriction is treated as a rights modification and is used only after the due process steps in RTS-02, including assessment, less intrusive methods, informed consent, time limits and review by the Human Rights Committee as required (GPR-02).
The Program Director keeps a supply of food and water to support the disaster preparedness plan (ENV-01).

The RN reviews diet orders, texture compliance, choking incidents and weights each month with the QIDP, and reports data to the QA committee (QA-01). The QIDP updates the Implementation Strategy as needs and preferences change.

Orders modified diets and recommends textures and precautions.
Checks food safety, posted diet sheets and food supplies; makes sure staff are trained.
